description: National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the licensed nurse or clinician who performed the triage assessment. Required for EMTALA compliance documentation and provider-level quality reporting. Sourced from Epic ClinDoc or Cerner PowerChart ED.
reference: EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; HIPAA NPI Final Rule 45 CFR §162.406; CMS NPI Registry

description: Indicates whether this triage record represents a reassessment of a previously triaged patient (e.g., patient condition changed while waiting). Supports tracking of acuity escalation events and waiting room safety monitoring.
reference: Joint Commission NPSG; AHRQ ED Safety Guidelines; Epic ClinDoc ED Module

description: Current workflow state of the triage assessment record. Indicates whether triage documentation is in progress, finalized, subsequently amended, or voided.
reference: Epic ClinDoc ED Module; HL7 FHIR R4 Encounter.status

description: Date and time when the triage assessment was initiated by the triage nurse. This is the principal business event timestamp used to calculate door-to-triage time and ED throughput quality measures.
reference: CMS ED Throughput Quality Measures; EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; Joint Commission NPSG

description: Patient weight measured or reported at triage, expressed in kilograms. Used for medication dosing calculations, pediatric weight-based protocols, and clinical decision support. PHI under HIPAA.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; LOINC 29463-7; Joint Commission Medication Management Standards

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each visit diagnosis record in the Silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this encounter-level diagnosis entity. Role: TRANSACTION_LINE — this record is a line-level diagnosis attached to a parent encounter/visit header.
reference: HL7 FHIR R4 Condition Resource; Epic ClinDoc Diagnosis Record

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.audit_finding. Business justification: Audit findings frequently cite specific diagnosis coding errors (upcoding, specificity, POA indicator errors). Direct linkage enables traceability from finding to the exact diagnosis record under revi

Reference to the attending physician responsible for the patient's care during this encounter, as associated with this diagnosis. Used for provider-level quality reporting, MIPS attribution, and UB-04 claim form population. Aligns with PARTY_REFERENCE canonical category.
reference: CMS UHDDS Attending Physician Definition; UB-04 FL 76; MIPS Attribution Rules; CMS

description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Diagnosis coding drives reimbursement and HCC risk adjustment. Linking to cost centers enables service-line profitability analysis, clinical program financial performance, and diagnosis-related cost b

Foreign key linking to reference.icd_code. Business justification: Core clinical coding workflow—every diagnosis on a visit must reference the official ICD-10 code set for billing compliance, quality reporting, HCC risk adjustment, and clinical documentation integrit

Reference to the patient associated with this visit diagnosis. Supports patient-level longitudinal diagnosis history, population health analytics, and risk adjustment. Classified as restricted PHI per HIPAA.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; HL7 FHIR R4 Patient Resource; Epic MPI

description: Reference to the clinical note or documentation that supports this diagnosis. Links the coded diagnosis back to the source clinical documentation for CDI, audit, and RAC defense purposes. Sourced from Epic ClinDoc.
reference: AHIMA CDI; OIG RAC Audit; HL7 FHIR R4 Condition.evidence; Epic ClinDoc

description: Foreign key linking to reference.snomed_concept. Business justification: Clinical terminology mapping—SNOMED codes on diagnoses must reference the official SNOMED CT concept for interoperability, clinical decision support, quality measure reporting, and data exchange with

Foreign key reference to the parent encounter/visit record. Establishes the HEADER_REFERENCE relationship linking this diagnosis line to its owning visit. Central to DRG grouping, quality reporting, and revenue cycle processing.
reference: HL7 FHIR R4 Encounter Resource; Epic ClinDoc; CMS Claim Encounter Linkage

description: Indicates whether this diagnosis code is included on the claim submitted to the payer. True = included on the claim. Some diagnoses may be documented clinically but excluded from billing (e.g., working diagnoses, non-billable codes). Drives UB-04 and CMS-1500 claim form population.
reference: CMS Claim Submission Guidelines; UB-04 FL 67; CMS-1500 Box 21; AHIMA Coding Guidelines

description: Classifies this diagnosis as a Complication/Comorbidity (CC), Major Complication/Comorbidity (MCC), Hospital-Acquired Condition (HAC), or none. Directly impacts MS-DRG assignment and inpatient reimbursement under IPPS. Sourced from 3M HIS grouper output and CMS CC/MCC exclusion lists.
reference: CMS MS-DRG Definitions Manual; 3M HIS Grouper; CMS IPPS; HAC Reduction Program

description: Indicates whether this diagnosis represents a chronic condition as defined by CMS Chronic Condition Warehouse (CCW) or clinical classification standards. True = chronic condition. Supports population health management, care management program enrollment, HEDIS chronic disease measure attribution, and SDOH analysis.
reference: CMS Chronic Condition Warehouse (CCW); NCQA HEDIS Chronic Disease Measures; AHRQ Clinical Classifications Software

description: The date on which the ICD-10-CM code was assigned to this diagnosis by the HIM coding team. Used for coding productivity tracking, CDI program metrics, and revenue cycle timeliness reporting. Sourced from 3M HIS and Epic Resolute coding workflows.
reference: AHIMA Coding Productivity Standards; 3M HIS; CMS Timely Filing Requirements

description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the clinician or coder who assigned or attested this diagnosis code. Used for audit trails, CDI accountability, RAC audit defense, and provider-level coding quality reporting. Sourced from 3M HIS and Epic ClinDoc coding workflows.
reference: CMS NPI Final Rule 45 CFR Part 162; HIPAA Administrative Simplification; OIG Compliance; 3M HIS

description: Current workflow status of this diagnosis record within the HIM/CDI coding lifecycle. 'pending' indicates awaiting coder review; 'coded' indicates initial code assignment; 'validated' indicates coder-confirmed; 'queried' indicates a CDI query has been issued; 'amended' indicates a post-bill correction; 'final' indicates billing-ready. Drives revenue cycle workflow and CDI query management in 3M HIS and Epic Resolute.
reference: AHIMA Coding Guidelines; 3M HIS CDI Workflow; CMS RAC Audit Requirements; OIG Compliance

description: The timestamp when this visit diagnosis record was first created in the source system or ingested into the Silver layer. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED canonical category requirement.
reference: HIPAA Audit Controls 45 CFR §164.312(b); HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; SOC 2

description: Clinical ranking of this diagnosis by severity or clinical significance within the encounter, as assigned by the coding team or clinical documentation system. Distinct from diagnosis_seq_num (billing sequence); this rank reflects clinical priority for care management and quality reporting purposes.
reference: AHIMA Clinical Documentation Improvement; 3M HIS CDI; Epic ClinDoc

description: Ordinal position of this diagnosis within the encounter's diagnosis list. Sequence 1 typically denotes the principal diagnosis. Used for claim form ordering (UB-04 diagnosis fields), DRG grouping logic, and quality measure attribution. Aligns with LINE_SEQUENCE canonical category.
reference: CMS UHDDS; UB-04 Claim Form FL 67; CMS-1500 Box 21; 3M HIS Grouper

description: Identifies who or what originated this diagnosis record. 'physician' = entered by the treating clinician; 'coder' = assigned by HIM coding staff; 'cdi_specialist' = added via CDI query resolution; 'system' = auto-populated by clinical decision support; 'imported' = received via HIE or external system. Supports audit trail and coding accountability.
reference: AHIMA CDI Practice Standards; OIG Compliance; HL7 FHIR R4 Condition.recorder; Epic ClinDoc

description: Classification of the diagnosis role within the encounter. 'admitting' is the reason for admission; 'principal' is the condition chiefly responsible for the stay after study; 'secondary' are comorbidities and complications; 'discharge' is the final coded diagnosis at discharge; 'working' is a provisional diagnosis during the encounter; 'final' is the confirmed diagnosis post-workup. Drives DRG assignment and UB-04/CMS-1500 claim form population.
reference: CMS Uniform Hospital Discharge Data Set (UHDDS); UB-04 Claim Form; CMS-1500; UHDDS Principal Diagnosis Definition

description: The MS-DRG or APR-DRG code assigned to the encounter as influenced by this diagnosis. Populated after DRG grouping by 3M HIS or CMS grouper. Central to inpatient reimbursement under IPPS and case mix index (CMI) calculation.
reference: CMS MS-DRG Definitions Manual; 3M APR-DRG Grouper; CMS IPPS; UB-04 FL 71

description: Indicates whether this diagnosis code contributes to the DRG assignment for this encounter. True = this diagnosis is a complication/comorbidity (CC) or major complication/comorbidity (MCC) that affects DRG grouping and reimbursement. Critical for revenue cycle optimization and CDI program targeting.
reference: CMS MS-DRG Grouper; 3M APR-DRG; CMS IPPS; UHDDS CC/MCC Definitions

description: Specifies the DRG classification system used: MS-DRG (Medicare Severity DRG, CMS), APR-DRG (All Patient Refined DRG, 3M), or IR-DRG (International Refined DRG). Determines the reimbursement methodology and payer applicability.
reference: CMS MS-DRG; 3M APR-DRG; WHO IR-DRG; CMS IPPS

description: Free-text clinical comment or qualifier associated with this diagnosis record, as entered by the coding team or clinician. May include specificity notes, CDI query resolution rationale, or coding clarifications. Classified as restricted PHI per HIPAA.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; AHIMA CDI; Epic ClinDoc; 3M HIS

description: The native identifier for this diagnosis record in the source operational system (e.g., Epic ClinDoc diagnosis ID or Cerner PowerChart diagnosis ID). Supports ETL lineage, data reconciliation, and source system audit trails in the Silver layer.
reference: Epic ClinDoc; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HL7 FHIR R4; HITRUST CSF Data Lineage

description: ICD-10-CM external cause code (V, W, X, Y codes) documenting the cause, place of occurrence, activity, and status for injury and poisoning diagnoses. Required for trauma registries, injury surveillance, workers' compensation claims, and public health reporting.
reference: ICD-10-CM External Cause Codes (V00-Y99); CMS Coding Guidelines; AHRQ Injury Surveillance; State Trauma Registry Requirements

description: Indicates whether this diagnosis represents a healthcare-associated infection (HAI) such as CLABSI, CAUTI, or SSI. True = HAI diagnosis. Triggers HAI surveillance workflows, CMS HAC Reduction Program payment adjustments, and TJC infection control reporting.
reference: CMS HAC Reduction Program; The Joint Commission Infection Control Standards; CDC NHSN HAI Definitions; AHRQ

description: The specific CMS HCC category code to which this ICD-10-CM diagnosis maps. Populated only when hcc_flag is True. Used for risk score calculation in Medicare Advantage, ACO, and MIPS/APM programs. Sourced from CMS HCC mapping crosswalk tables.
reference: CMS HCC Risk Adjustment Model V28; CMS-HCC Crosswalk; MACRA; CMS Medicare Advantage

description: Indicates whether this ICD-10-CM diagnosis code maps to a CMS Hierarchical Condition Category (HCC) used for risk adjustment in Medicare Advantage and ACO programs. True = this diagnosis contributes to the patient's HCC risk score. Critical for population health management, value-based care contracting, and capitation payment accuracy.
reference: CMS HCC Risk Adjustment Model; CMS-HCC V28; MACRA APM Framework; NCQA HEDIS

business_glossary_term: International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision (ICD-10) Code
description: The ICD-10-CM diagnosis code assigned to this visit. Drives DRG grouping, quality measure attribution, risk adjustment (HCC mapping), and medical billing. Sourced from Epic ClinDoc and validated through 3M HIS coding workflows. Conforms to WHO ICD-10-CM code format.
reference: WHO ICD-10-CM; CMS ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines; 3M HIS Grouping; AMA

business_glossary_term: International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision (ICD-10) Diagnosis Description
description: Full clinical description of the ICD-10-CM diagnosis code as defined by the WHO/CMS code set. Provides human-readable context for the coded diagnosis. Used in clinical documentation, reporting, and CDI workflows.
reference: WHO ICD-10-CM; CMS ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines; 3M HIS

description: The fiscal year version of the ICD-10-CM code set used to assign this diagnosis code (e.g., FY2024). ICD-10-CM is updated annually by CMS/CDC. Ensures accurate code interpretation across fiscal year transitions and supports historical data analysis.
reference: CMS ICD-10-CM Annual Updates; CDC ICD-10-CM Tabular List; WHO ICD-10

description: Indicates whether this diagnosis is classified as a mental health or behavioral health condition per ICD-10-CM Chapter 5 (F-codes). True = mental/behavioral health diagnosis. Supports behavioral health program management, parity compliance reporting, and population health segmentation.
reference: ICD-10-CM Chapter 5 Mental and Behavioral Disorders; Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA); CMS Behavioral Health Strategy

description: The date on which the diagnosed condition first manifested or was first identified, as documented in the clinical record. Supports longitudinal disease tracking, chronic condition management, POA determination, and population health analytics. Aligns with BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP canonical category.
reference: HL7 FHIR R4 Condition.onset; Epic ClinDoc; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

description: Indicates whether the diagnosis condition was present at the time of inpatient admission. Values: Y=Yes (present on admission), N=No (not present on admission), U=Unknown, W=Clinically undetermined, 1=Exempt from POA reporting. Required by CMS for inpatient claims on UB-04. Impacts HAI reporting, VBP penalties, and hospital-acquired condition (HAC) payment adjustments.
reference: CMS POA Reporting Guidelines; UB-04 FL 67 POA Indicator; IPPS HAC Reduction Program; The Joint Commission HAI Standards

description: Indicates whether this diagnosis is designated as the primary/principal diagnosis for the encounter. True = primary diagnosis. Provides a quick boolean filter for analytics and reporting without requiring sequence number logic. Complements diagnosis_seq_num and diagnosis_type.
reference: CMS UHDDS Principal Diagnosis Definition; UB-04 FL 67; AHIMA Coding Guidelines

description: Indicates whether this diagnosis contributes to one or more quality measure denominators or numerators (e.g., HEDIS, MIPS, VBP, TJC core measures). True = this diagnosis is relevant to at least one active quality measure. Supports quality reporting, MIPS scoring, and VBP program management.
reference: NCQA HEDIS; CMS MIPS; CMS VBP Program; The Joint Commission Core Measures; MACRA

description: Indicates whether this diagnosis is a notifiable/reportable condition requiring mandatory reporting to public health authorities (e.g., state health departments, CDC). True = reportable. Supports public health surveillance, regulatory compliance, and HIE reporting obligations.
reference: State Departments of Health Reportable Disease Lists; CDC National Notifiable Diseases; HIPAA Public Health Disclosure Exception 45 CFR §164.512(b)

description: The date on which the diagnosed condition was resolved, abated, or no longer active, as documented in the clinical record. Null if the condition is ongoing. Used for chronic disease management, care plan updates, and longitudinal patient health tracking.
reference: HL7 FHIR R4 Condition.abatement; Epic ClinDoc; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

description: Indicates whether this diagnosis code represents a Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) factor (e.g., Z-codes for housing instability, food insecurity, transportation barriers). True = SDOH-related diagnosis. Supports population health management, care coordination, and CMS SDOH reporting initiatives.
reference: CMS SDOH Strategy; ICD-10-CM Z-Codes for SDOH; AHRQ SDOH Framework; Healthy People 2030

business_glossary_term: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT) Code
description: The SNOMED CT concept identifier mapped to this ICD-10-CM diagnosis code. Supports clinical interoperability, HL7 FHIR-based HIE data exchange, and clinical decision support. Populated via ICD-10 to SNOMED CT crosswalk. Used in FHIR Condition resources for interoperability.
reference: SNOMED International; HL7 FHIR R4 Condition.code; NLM SNOMED CT US Edition; HHS Interoperability Rule

description: Indicates whether this diagnosis represents a substance use disorder (SUD) per ICD-10-CM codes. True = substance use disorder diagnosis. Supports SUD program management, 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality compliance, and population health analytics.
reference: ICD-10-CM SUD Codes; 42 CFR Part 2 (Confidentiality of SUD Records); SAMHSA; CMS Opioid Strategy

description: The timestamp when this visit diagnosis record was last modified in the source system or Silver layer. Supports change data capture, audit trail, and RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED canonical category requirement.
reference: HIPAA Audit Controls 45 CFR §164.312(b); HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; SOC 2

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each procedure record performed during a patient visit. Primary key for the visit_procedure data product in the encounter domain.

Foreign key linking to compliance.audit_finding. Business justification: Procedure coding audit findings (unbundling, medical necessity, modifier errors, upcoding) must reference the specific procedure record being challenged. Enables direct linkage from compliance finding

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Procedures are performed in specific departments/cost centers. Essential for activity-based costing, OR suite profitability analysis, procedural revenue tracking, and CPT-based cost allocation for dep

Foreign key linking to reference.cpt_code. Business justification: Essential procedure coding workflow—every CPT code on a visit procedure must validate against the official CPT reference for claims submission, reimbursement calculation, RVU assignment, and NCCI edit

Foreign key linking to reference.hcpcs_code. Business justification: Required for HCPCS procedure coding—DME, supplies, drugs, and non-physician services must reference official HCPCS codes for billing, coverage determination, and reimbursement. Critical for outpatient

Foreign key linking to reference.icd_code. Business justification: Inpatient procedure coding workflow—ICD-10-PCS codes must validate against the official ICD-10 code set for inpatient claims submission, DRG grouping, and quality measure reporting. Required for hospi

Foreign key linking to radiology.interventional_procedure. Business justification: Interventional radiology procedures (biopsies, drainages, embolizations) are billable encounter procedures requiring linkage for charge capture, procedural documentation, and outcomes tracking. IR pro

Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Procedures consume specific supplies, devices, and implants that must be documented for billing (CDM charge codes), regulatory compliance (UDI tracking for implantables), and procedure cost analysis.
Reference to the patient on whom the procedure was performed. Supports patient-level procedure history, quality measurement, and population health analytics.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; HL7 FHIR R4 Patient Resource; CMS Conditions of Participation

description: Reference to the operating room or procedure room where the procedure was performed. Supports OR utilization reporting, room turnover analysis, and facility capacity planning.
reference: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; The Joint Commission Environment of Care Standards

description: Reference to the clinician who performed the procedure. Used for provider-level quality reporting, credentialing validation, and RVU attribution.
reference: CMS NPI Registry; HL7 FHIR R4 Practitioner Resource; MIPS/MACRA Reporting

description: Foreign key linking to provider.privileging. Business justification: Enables retrospective verification that performing clinician held valid privileges for the specific procedure at the facility on the procedure date. Required for peer review, quality assurance audits,

Foreign key linking to research.research_study. Business justification: Research billing requires distinguishing study-mandated procedures from standard-of-care for coverage analysis and sponsor billing. Protocol compliance monitoring needs to verify required procedures w

Foreign key linking to reference.snomed_concept. Business justification: Procedure terminology mapping—SNOMED codes on procedures must reference official SNOMED CT for clinical documentation, interoperability, and data exchange with external systems. Required for USCDI com
Reference to the parent encounter/visit during which this procedure was performed. Links the procedure to the ADT event, visit type, and associated clinical and billing context.
reference: HL7 FHIR R4 Encounter Resource; Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet

description: Type of anesthesia administered during the procedure. Drives anesthesia CPT code selection, anesthesia time unit billing, ASA physical status documentation, and OR case complexity classification.
reference: AMA CPT Anesthesia Guidelines; ASA Physical Status Classification; Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet

business_glossary_term: American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) Physical Status Classification
description: ASA physical status classification assigned by the anesthesiologist prior to the procedure, reflecting the patient's overall health status. Used for anesthesia risk stratification, surgical case complexity scoring, and outcomes risk adjustment.
reference: ASA Physical Status Classification System; Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; AHRQ Risk Adjustment

description: Anatomical location or body site where the procedure was performed, coded using SNOMED CT body structure concepts. Supports surgical safety documentation, quality measure stratification, and clinical analytics.
reference: SNOMED CT Body Structure Hierarchy; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.bodySite; The Joint Commission Universal Protocol

description: Reason code or description explaining why a scheduled procedure was cancelled (e.g., patient not ready, equipment unavailable, surgeon unavailable, insurance denial). Populated only when is_cancelled is true. Supports root cause analysis and OR efficiency improvement.
reference: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; The Joint Commission OR Performance Metrics

description: Gross charge amount posted to the patient account for this procedure based on the CDM. Represents the billed amount before contractual adjustments, payer discounts, or patient responsibility. Used in revenue cycle management and financial reporting.
reference: CMS CDM; Epic Resolute HB/PB; Cerner Revenue Cycle; GAAP/FASB Revenue Recognition

description: Internal charge code from the Charge Description Master (CDM) mapped to this procedure. Links the clinical procedure to the revenue cycle for charge capture, pricing, and claim generation in Epic Resolute or Cerner Revenue Cycle.
reference: CMS CDM Requirements; Epic Resolute HB/PB; Cerner Revenue Cycle; OIG Compliance Guidance

description: Free-text or coded description of the complication that occurred during or after the procedure. Populated only when complication_flag is true. Used for clinical documentation, quality review, and risk management reporting.
reference: AHRQ PSI; CMS VBP; CDC NHSN; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.complication

description: Indicates whether a complication was documented as occurring during or immediately following the procedure. Triggers CDI query workflow, quality event review, and HAI/PSI surveillance reporting.
reference: AHRQ Patient Safety Indicators (PSI); CMS VBP; CDC NHSN; The Joint Commission

description: Indicates whether informed consent was documented as obtained from the patient or legal guardian prior to the procedure. Required for regulatory compliance, malpractice risk management, and The Joint Commission accreditation standards.
reference: The Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.13; EMTALA

description: AMA CPT code identifying the procedure for professional billing, charge capture, and payer adjudication. Required on CMS-1500 claims. Drives RVU calculation and reimbursement.
reference: AMA CPT Coding Standards; CMS-1500; CMS Physician Fee Schedule

description: Primary CPT modifier appended to the procedure code to indicate special circumstances (e.g., 50=bilateral, LT=left side, RT=right side, 22=increased procedural services, 59=distinct procedural service). Required for accurate claim adjudication.
reference: AMA CPT Modifier Guidelines; CMS-1500; CMS Correct Coding Initiative (CCI)

description: Secondary CPT modifier providing additional claim specificity when a single modifier is insufficient. Used in conjunction with cpt_modifier_1 for complex billing scenarios per CMS Correct Coding Initiative.
reference: AMA CPT Modifier Guidelines; CMS-1500; CMS Correct Coding Initiative (CCI)

description: Timestamp when this procedure record was first created in the source system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and regulatory compliance documentation per HIPAA and The Joint Commission medical record requirements.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; The Joint Commission MR.01.01.01; ISO 27001

description: Indicates whether this procedure influences the DRG assignment for the inpatient encounter. Flagged by the 3M grouper or equivalent DRG grouping engine. Critical for inpatient revenue integrity and CDI prioritization.
reference: CMS IPPS DRG Grouping; 3M Health Information Systems Grouping; CMS MS-DRG Definitions Manual

business_glossary_term: Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Code
description: HCPCS Level II code used when a CPT code is not applicable, primarily for supplies, durable medical equipment, and non-physician services billed to Medicare/Medicaid. Complements CPT on UB-04 and CMS-1500 claims.
reference: CMS HCPCS Coding; UB-04; CMS-1500; CMS Conditions of Participation

description: ICD-10-PCS code assigned for inpatient procedures. Required for inpatient DRG grouping, UB-04 institutional claims, and CMS inpatient prospective payment system (IPPS) reimbursement. Not applicable for outpatient encounters.
reference: WHO ICD-10-PCS; CMS IPPS; UB-04; 3M Health Information Systems Grouping

description: Indicates whether a medical device or implant was used during the procedure. Triggers UDI (Unique Device Identifier) documentation requirements per FDA regulations and supply chain charge capture workflows.
reference: FDA UDI Rule 21 CFR Part 830; The Joint Commission; CMS Conditions of Participation; Infor Lawson Supply Chain

description: Indicates whether a scheduled procedure was cancelled before execution. Used for OR cancellation rate reporting, scheduling efficiency analysis, and revenue impact assessment.
reference: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; The Joint Commission OR Performance Metrics

description: Indicates whether the procedure was scheduled as elective (non-urgent) versus emergent or urgent. Supports surgical scheduling analytics, OR block time management, and payer prior authorization workflows.
reference: CMS Elective Surgery Definitions; Epic Cadence; Cerner SurgiNet Scheduling

description: Indicates whether this is the principal procedure performed for the encounter, as defined by the Uniform Hospital Discharge Data Set (UHDDS). The principal procedure is the one most closely related to the principal diagnosis and drives DRG assignment for inpatient cases.
reference: CMS UHDDS; CMS IPPS; UB-04 FL 74; 3M Health Information Systems Grouping

description: Body side on which the procedure was performed. Required for correct CPT modifier assignment (RT/LT/50), surgical safety checklists, and wrong-site surgery prevention per The Joint Commission Universal Protocol.
reference: AMA CPT Modifiers RT/LT/50; The Joint Commission Universal Protocol; CMS-1500; UB-04

description: 10-digit NPI of the performing provider as required on CMS-1500 and UB-04 claims. Stored denormalized here for claim generation and audit purposes, as the NPI is a regulatory billing requirement independent of the provider master record.
reference: CMS NPI Final Rule 45 CFR Part 162; CMS-1500 Box 24J; UB-04 FL 56; HIPAA

description: Calendar date on which the procedure was performed. Used for charge capture date-of-service, quality measure denominator identification, and surgical case scheduling analytics.
reference: CMS Conditions of Participation; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.performed[x]; AMA CPT

description: Full clinical description of the procedure as documented in the source system (Epic ClinDoc, OpTime, or Cerner SurgiNet). Provides human-readable context for the CPT/HCPCS/ICD-10-PCS code.
reference: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.code.text

description: Date and time when the procedure was completed (closure for surgical cases, or final clinical action for non-surgical). Combined with start timestamp to derive procedure duration for OR utilization and case costing.
reference: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; The Joint Commission OR Metrics

description: Externally visible, human-readable identifier assigned to this procedure record within the source system (e.g., Epic OpTime case number or Cerner SurgiNet procedure order number). Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit.
reference: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.identifier

description: Date and time when the procedure began (knife-to-skin for surgical cases, or first clinical action for non-surgical). Used for OR utilization analysis, case duration calculation, and scheduling efficiency reporting.
reference: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; The Joint Commission OR Metrics

description: Current workflow status of the procedure record per HL7 FHIR Procedure.status value set. Drives charge capture eligibility, quality measure inclusion/exclusion, and CDI workflow routing.
reference: HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.status; Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet

description: High-level classification of the procedure category. Supports operational reporting, OR scheduling, charge master (CDM) mapping, and departmental cost allocation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: surgical|diagnostic|therapeutic|anesthesia|radiology|laboratory|nursing|other — promote to reference product]
reference: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; CMS CDM; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.category

description: Number of times this procedure was performed or units billed within the encounter. Used for charge capture accuracy, claim line quantity reporting, and utilization analysis.
reference: AMA CPT Billing Guidelines; CMS-1500 Box 24G; UB-04 FL 46

description: Total RVU for the procedure, comprising work RVU, practice expense RVU, and malpractice RVU components per the CMS Physician Fee Schedule. Used for overall provider productivity benchmarking and reimbursement modeling.
reference: CMS Physician Fee Schedule; MACRA/MIPS; AMA RVU Update Committee (RUC)

description: Physician work RVU assigned to this procedure per the CMS Physician Fee Schedule. Represents the time, skill, and intensity of the physician's work. Used for provider productivity measurement, compensation modeling, and MIPS performance reporting.
reference: CMS Physician Fee Schedule; MACRA/MIPS; AMA RVU Update Committee (RUC)

description: Ordinal position of this procedure within the encounter, used to distinguish principal from secondary procedures on claims. Sequence 1 typically denotes the principal procedure for DRG grouping and IPPS reimbursement.
reference: CMS IPPS DRG Grouping; UB-04 FL 74; 3M Health Information Systems Grouping

business_glossary_term: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT) Procedure Code
description: SNOMED CT concept identifier for the procedure, providing a clinically precise, interoperable representation beyond CPT/ICD-10-PCS. Supports HIE data exchange, FHIR-based interoperability, and clinical decision support.
reference: SNOMED International; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.code; ONC Interoperability Rule

description: Native identifier of this procedure record in the originating source system (e.g., Epic OpTime case ID, Cerner SurgiNet order ID). Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational EHR system.
reference: HITRUST CSF; HL7 FHIR R4 Provenance Resource; Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet

description: Method or technique used to access the operative site. Drives ICD-10-PCS character 5 (approach) coding, surgical case complexity classification, and outcomes benchmarking.
reference: ICD-10-PCS Approach Character; Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; AHRQ Quality Indicators

description: Indicates whether the pre-procedure surgical time-out (Universal Protocol) was performed and documented, confirming correct patient, site, and procedure. Required by The Joint Commission Universal Protocol for preventing wrong-site surgery.
reference: The Joint Commission Universal Protocol UP.01.03.01; CMS Conditions of Participation; AHRQ Patient Safety

description: FDA-assigned Unique Device Identifier for any medical device or implant used during the procedure. Required for FDA MDR (Medical Device Reporting), recall management, and supply chain traceability. Populated only when implant_flag is true.
reference: FDA UDI Rule 21 CFR Part 830; FDA GUDID Database; The Joint Commission; CMS Conditions of Participation

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this procedure record in the source system. Supports incremental ETL processing, change data capture, and audit trail requirements for medical record integrity.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; The Joint Commission MR.01.01.01; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF

description: CDC wound classification assigned at the time of surgery, indicating the degree of microbial contamination. Used for SSI (Surgical Site Infection) risk stratification, HAI surveillance, and quality reporting to NHSN.
reference: CDC NHSN SSI Surveillance; The Joint Commission; AHRQ Patient Safety Indicators; CMS VBP

The dollar threshold above which a case qualifies for additional outlier payment. Calculated as: (DRG payment × fixed loss ratio) + fixed loss amount.
The timestamp when this DRG record was first created in the reference data system. Used for data lineage and historical analysis.
The official numeric code assigned to this DRG by the grouper system (e.g., 470, 871). Used as the business identifier for reimbursement and case mix reporting.
Extended narrative description of the DRG, including clinical context, typical procedures, and coding guidance. Used for clinical documentation improvement (CDI) and coder education.
Classification of the DRG as medical (non-surgical), surgical, or procedure-based. Used for service line segmentation and resource planning.
The date on which this DRG definition and relative weight became effective (typically October 1 of the fiscal year).
The date on which this DRG definition and relative weight expire (typically September 30 of the fiscal year). Null for currently active DRGs.
The geometric mean length of stay in days for cases in this DRG, calculated from national claims data. Used as the threshold for identifying outlier cases and calculating outlier payments.
The DRG grouper classification system under which this DRG is defined: MS-DRG (Medicare Severity), AP-DRG (All Patient), APR-DRG (All Patient Refined), or IR-DRG (International Refined).
reference: CMS MS-DRG Grouper, 3M Health Information Systems APR-DRG

description: The timestamp when this DRG record was last modified in the reference data system. Used for change tracking and audit trails.
The national average total charges (not payments) for cases in this DRG. Used for charge benchmarking and cost-to-charge ratio analysis.
The national average Medicare payment amount for this DRG, calculated as: national base rate × relative weight. Used for benchmarking and financial forecasting.
The total number of Medicare cases nationally that grouped to this DRG in the most recent fiscal year. Used for prevalence analysis and market sizing.
Indicates whether this DRG is classified as an OR procedure DRG, which affects payment and resource allocation.

Indicates whether this DRG is subject to the post-acute care transfer policy, which adjusts payment when a patient is discharged to a post-acute care setting (SNF, IRF, LTCH, HHA) before the geometric mean LOS.
The ending ICD-10-CM diagnosis code in the range of principal diagnoses that can group to this DRG.
reference: CMS ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines, MS-DRG Grouper Logic

description: The starting ICD-10-CM diagnosis code in the range of principal diagnoses that can group to this DRG. Used for grouper logic validation and clinical documentation improvement.
reference: CMS ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines, MS-DRG Grouper Logic

description: Indicates whether this DRG requires the presence of a specific ICD-10-PCS procedure code to group (true for surgical DRGs, false for medical DRGs).
Indicates whether this DRG is associated with specific quality measures under the Hospital Value-Based Purchasing (VBP) or Hospital-Acquired Condition (HAC) Reduction Programs.
Indicates whether this DRG is included in the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP) and subject to payment penalties for excess readmissions.

The DRG relative weight representing the average resource intensity for cases in this DRG compared to the national average (1.0000). Used to calculate expected reimbursement: base rate × relative weight.
Indicates whether this DRG has special payment rules or adjustments (e.g., new technology add-on payments, device-intensive procedures).
The full descriptive title of the DRG (e.g., 'Major Hip and Knee Joint Replacement or Reattachment of Lower Extremity with MCC').

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Code ID
description: Unique identifier for the HCPCS code record. Primary key.

Foreign key linking to reference.code_set_version. Business justification: HCPCS Level II codes are maintained by CMS with annual updates and quarterly releases. The hcpcs_code table has version_year (INT) and status attributes that should be normalized to code_set_version f
Indicates any age-based coverage restrictions for this HCPCS code (e.g., pediatric only, adult only, age 65+). Defines patient age eligibility criteria.
The base unit value assigned to anesthesia-related HCPCS codes, used in calculating anesthesia reimbursement. Null for non-anesthesia codes.
reference: CMS Physician Fee Schedule, ASA Relative Value Guide

description: Indicates the payment methodology for this HCPCS code when performed in an Ambulatory Surgical Center setting. Defines whether the code is separately payable, bundled, or excluded from ASC payment.
Indicates whether an assistant surgeon is allowed for this HCPCS code and the applicable payment percentage for assistant surgeon services.
Indicates whether this HCPCS code is eligible for bilateral surgery payment adjustment when performed on both sides of the body during the same operative session.
Indicates whether co-surgeons are allowed for this HCPCS code, where two surgeons perform distinct portions of a complex procedure.

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Code Type
description: Classification of the code lifecycle: permanent codes are established in the annual update, temporary codes are used for emerging technology or services, deleted codes are no longer valid.
reference: CMS HCPCS Level II Coding Manual

description: Indicates whether the HCPCS code is covered by Medicare: covered codes are reimbursable, not_covered codes are excluded, carrier_discretion allows local Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) determination, bundled codes are included in other services, conditional codes require specific clinical criteria.
reference: CMS National Coverage Determinations (NCD), CMS Local Coverage Determinations (LCD)

description: Indicates whether this HCPCS code requires specific ICD-10 diagnosis codes for coverage. True if diagnosis-based medical necessity criteria apply, false otherwise.
reference: CMS National Coverage Determinations (NCD), CMS Local Coverage Determinations (LCD)

description: Indicates whether this HCPCS code represents durable medical equipment as defined by Medicare. True for DME items (typically E-codes), false for other categories.
Indicates whether this HCPCS code represents a pharmaceutical drug or biological product (typically J-codes). True for drug codes, false for equipment, supplies, and services.
reference: CMS HCPCS Level II Coding Manual

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Effective Date
description: The date on which this HCPCS code became valid and available for use in billing and claims submission.
reference: CMS HCPCS Level II Coding Manual

description: The maximum frequency at which this HCPCS code can be billed (e.g., once per year, once per lifetime, twice per month). Defines time-based coverage restrictions.
reference: CMS National Coverage Determinations (NCD), CMS Local Coverage Determinations (LCD)

description: Indicates any gender-based restrictions for this HCPCS code. Some codes are specific to male or female anatomy; most have no restriction.
reference: CMS HCPCS Level II Coding Manual

description: The number of days of post-operative care included in the payment for this HCPCS code (e.g., 000, 010, 090, XXX, YYY, ZZZ). Defines the global surgical package period.
reference: CMS Physician Fee Schedule, Global Surgery Policy

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Category
description: The major category of the HCPCS code based on the first letter: A=Transportation/Medical Supplies, B=Enteral/Parenteral, C=Outpatient PPS, D=Dental, E=DME, G=Temporary Procedures, H=Alcohol/Drug, J=Drugs, K=Temporary Codes, L=Orthotics/Prosthetics, M=Medical Services, P=Pathology/Lab, Q=Temporary Codes, R=Diagnostic Radiology, S=Private Payer, T=State Medicaid, V=Vision/Hearing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: A|B|C|D|E|G|H|J|K|L|M|P|Q|R|S|T|V — 17 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: CMS HCPCS Level II Coding Manual

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Code
description: The five-character alphanumeric HCPCS Level II code (e.g., E0601, J1234). First character is always a letter (A-V), followed by four digits. Used to identify durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics, supplies, drugs, and non-physician services.
reference: CMS HCPCS Level II Coding Manual

description: The percentage of the total payment allocated to intraoperative services for this HCPCS code within the global surgical package.
The date on which this HCPCS code record was last modified in the reference data system, reflecting the most recent change to code attributes, descriptions, or coverage indicators.

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Long Description
description: Full detailed description of the HCPCS code, providing comprehensive information about the item, service, drug, or supply represented by the code.
reference: CMS HCPCS Level II Coding Manual

description: Indicates whether a modifier is required when billing this HCPCS code. True if a modifier is mandatory for proper claims adjudication, false otherwise.
reference: CMS HCPCS Level II Coding Manual

description: Indicates whether and how payment adjustments apply when this HCPCS code is billed with other procedures on the same date of service. Defines reduction percentages for subsequent procedures.
reference: CMS Physician Fee Schedule, Multiple Procedure Payment Reduction (MPPR) Policy

description: Indicates whether this HCPCS code has an associated NDC crosswalk mapping. True for drug codes that map to specific NDC products, false otherwise.

business_glossary_term: OPPS (Outpatient Prospective Payment System) Payment Indicator
description: Indicates the payment status for this HCPCS code under the Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System. Defines whether the code is separately payable, packaged, or excluded from OPPS payment.
Indicates any restrictions on where this HCPCS code may be performed or billed (e.g., inpatient only, outpatient only, office only). Defines valid place of service codes.
reference: CMS Place of Service Codes, 42 CFR 414

description: The percentage of the total payment allocated to postoperative services for this HCPCS code within the global surgical package.
The percentage of the total payment allocated to preoperative services for this HCPCS code within the global surgical package.

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Pricing Indicator
description: Indicates the pricing methodology for the HCPCS code: fee_schedule uses CMS published rates, asc uses Ambulatory Surgical Center payment, reasonable_charge uses historical pricing, not_priced has no established rate, contractor_priced is determined by local MAC.
reference: CMS Physician Fee Schedule, CMS ASC Payment System

description: Indicates whether this HCPCS code requires prior authorization from the payer before services can be rendered. True if pre-approval is required, false otherwise.
Indicates whether this HCPCS code has separate professional and technical components (e.g., for radiology and pathology services). Defines billing options for split or global billing.
The maximum allowable quantity of this HCPCS code that can be billed per claim, per day, or per time period as defined by coverage policy. Null if no limit applies.
reference: CMS National Coverage Determinations (NCD), CMS Local Coverage Determinations (LCD)

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Short Description
description: Abbreviated description of the HCPCS code, typically 28 characters or less, used for display on claims and billing screens.
reference: CMS HCPCS Level II Coding Manual

business_glossary_term: Superseded By HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Code
description: The HCPCS code that replaces this code if it has been superseded or deleted. Null for active codes that have not been replaced.
reference: CMS HCPCS Level II Coding Manual

description: Indicates whether team surgery is allowed for this HCPCS code, where multiple surgeons of different specialties are medically necessary.
Indicates whether this HCPCS code includes a technical component representing facility resources, equipment, and supplies.

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Termination Date
description: The date on which this HCPCS code was discontinued or replaced. Null for currently active codes.
reference: CMS HCPCS Level II Coding Manual

description: The standard unit of measure for billing this HCPCS code (e.g., each, milligram, milliliter, hour, day, unit). Defines the quantity increment for claims submission.
reference: CMS HCPCS Level II Coding Manual

business_glossary_term: ICD (International Classification of Diseases) Code ID
description: Unique identifier for the ICD code record. Primary key.

Foreign key linking to reference.code_set_version. Business justification: ICD-10-CM and ICD-10-PCS codes are published annually by CMS with version-specific effective/expiration dates. The icd_code table has version (STRING) and status attributes that should be normalized t
The maximum patient age (in years) for which this ICD code is clinically appropriate. Used for coding validation and quality checks. Null if no maximum age restriction applies.
The minimum patient age (in years) for which this ICD code is clinically appropriate. Used for coding validation and quality checks. Null if no minimum age restriction applies.

Indicates whether this ICD code is valid for billing and reimbursement purposes. Only billable codes may be submitted on claims to payers. Non-billable codes are typically higher-level category codes used for classification only.
Indicates whether this diagnosis code is classified as a Complication or Comorbidity (CC) for DRG assignment and severity adjustment purposes.

The ICD-10 chapter to which this code belongs, representing the highest-level clinical category (e.g., Chapter 1: Certain infectious and parasitic diseases, Chapter 9: Diseases of the circulatory system).

business_glossary_term: ICD (International Classification of Diseases) Chapter Code Range
description: The alphanumeric range defining the chapter boundaries (e.g., A00-B99 for infectious diseases). Used for hierarchical grouping and reporting.

business_glossary_term: ICD (International Classification of Diseases) Code Type
description: Indicates whether this code represents a diagnosis (ICD-10-CM) or a procedure (ICD-10-PCS).
The date and time when this ICD code record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
The date on which this ICD code became valid for use in clinical documentation, billing, and reporting. Aligns with annual CMS ICD-10 update cycles (typically October 1).
Indicates whether this code represents the underlying etiology or cause of a condition and should be sequenced before manifestation codes per ICD-10-CM coding conventions.
The date on which this ICD code was retired or replaced and is no longer valid for use. Null for currently active codes.
Indicates whether this ICD code is applicable only to male patients, only to female patients, or to both. Used for clinical validation and coding accuracy.
Indicates whether this diagnosis code represents a Hospital-Acquired Condition (HAC) as defined by CMS. HACs may result in payment penalties under the Hospital-Acquired Condition Reduction Program.
The three-character category code representing a group of related conditions or procedures within a chapter (e.g., A01 for typhoid and paratyphoid fevers).
The full ICD-10-CM diagnosis code or ICD-10-PCS procedure code as published by WHO and maintained by CMS. Format follows alphanumeric pattern with optional decimal subdivision (e.g., A01.0, Z99.89).

business_glossary_term: ICD (International Classification of Diseases) Code Long Description
description: Full clinical description of the diagnosis or procedure code, providing comprehensive detail for clinical documentation, coding accuracy, and medical record completeness.
Indicates whether this code represents a manifestation of an underlying disease and must be sequenced after the underlying condition code per ICD-10-CM coding conventions.

Indicates whether this diagnosis code is classified as a Major Complication or Comorbidity (MCC) for DRG assignment and severity adjustment purposes. MCCs have greater impact on reimbursement than standard CCs.

business_glossary_term: Parent ICD (International Classification of Diseases) Code
description: The immediate parent code in the ICD-10 hierarchy, enabling hierarchical rollup and drill-down navigation for reporting and analytics.
Indicates whether this diagnosis code is exempt from the CMS Present on Admission (POA) reporting requirement for inpatient claims. POA-exempt codes do not require a POA indicator on UB-04 claims.

business_glossary_term: Replacement ICD (International Classification of Diseases) Code
description: The ICD code that replaces this code if the code has been retired or superseded. Used for code mapping and historical claims reprocessing.

business_glossary_term: ICD (International Classification of Diseases) Code Short Description
description: Abbreviated clinical description of the diagnosis or procedure code, typically used in constrained display contexts such as billing forms and summary reports.

business_glossary_term: SNOMED CT (Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms) Mapping
description: The corresponding SNOMED CT concept identifier(s) mapped to this ICD code, enabling interoperability with clinical terminology systems and EHR platforms.
reference: SNOMED International ICD-10 to SNOMED CT Map

description: The four-character subcategory code providing additional clinical specificity within a category (e.g., A01.0 for typhoid fever).
Indicates whether this diagnosis code is prohibited from being used as the principal diagnosis on an inpatient claim per CMS coding guidelines.
The date and time when this ICD code record was last modified in the system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.
Indicates whether this code is valid for use in clinical documentation and coding. Codes may be invalid due to retirement, replacement, or administrative reasons.

business_glossary_term: LOINC (Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes) Code ID
description: Unique identifier for the LOINC code record. Primary key.

Foreign key linking to reference.code_set_version. Business justification: LOINC codes are maintained by Regenstrief Institute with biannual releases. The loinc_code table has version_first_released (STRING), version_last_changed (STRING), and status attributes that should b
The high-level category or domain of the observation (e.g., CHEM=Chemistry, HEM/BC=Hematology/Blood Count, MICRO=Microbiology, RAD=Radiology, VITALS=Vital Signs).
The substance or entity being measured or observed (e.g., Glucose, Hemoglobin, Creatinine). This is the analyte, the target of the measurement.
A patient-friendly, lay-language name for the observation or test, used in patient portals and consumer-facing applications.
The date and time when this LOINC code record was first created in the system. Audit trail field.
The date when this LOINC code was deprecated or retired. Null if the code is still active.
The preferred display name for this LOINC code in the current implementation. May be customized by the organization while maintaining the standard LOINC number.
The date when this LOINC code became active and available for use in clinical systems.

business_glossary_term: Example UCUM (Unified Code for Units of Measure) Units
description: The standardized UCUM representation of the example units. Used for interoperability and unit conversion.
reference: UCUM (Unified Code for Units of Measure)

description: Common units of measure for this observation (e.g., mg/dL, mmol/L, %). Provides guidance for result reporting.
reference: Regenstrief Institute LOINC Standard, UCUM (Unified Code for Units of Measure)

description: Copyright or licensing information for LOINC codes that incorporate third-party content (e.g., SNOMED CT, CPT). Required for compliance with external terminology licenses.
reference: Regenstrief Institute LOINC Standard, Third-Party Terminology Licenses

business_glossary_term: HL7 (Health Level Seven) Field Subfield ID
description: The HL7 v2.x message field identifier where this LOINC code is typically used (e.g., OBX-3 for observation identifier). Supports HL7 message mapping.

business_glossary_term: HL7 (Health Level Seven) Version 3 Code System OID (Object Identifier)
description: The HL7 v3 object identifier for the LOINC code system (typically 2.16.840.1.113883.6.1). Used in CDA documents and HL7 v3 messages.
Boolean flag indicating whether this LOINC code is currently active and available for use in the organization. True=active, False=inactive or deprecated locally.
The date when this LOINC code mapping was last reviewed and verified by clinical informatics or laboratory staff. Supports ongoing terminology governance.
Organization-specific internal code or identifier mapped to this LOINC code. Used for legacy system integration and local terminology management.

business_glossary_term: LOINC (Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes) Number
description: The unique LOINC code identifier assigned by Regenstrief Institute. Format: numeric-numeric (e.g., 2345-7). This is the authoritative external identifier for the observation or test.
The full, human-readable display name for the LOINC code. This is the primary display term used in clinical systems and reports.
The method or technique used to make the observation or measurement (e.g., Electrophoresis, Immunoassay, Microscopy). May be null if method is not specified.
Indicates whether this LOINC code is used for ordering tests, recording observations, or both. Order=orderable panel or test, Observation=result only, Both=can be used for ordering and results.
Indicates if this LOINC code represents a panel (group of related tests), battery (predefined test group), or set (collection of observations). Null for individual observations.
The characteristic or attribute of the analyte being measured (e.g., Mass Concentration, Substance Concentration, Presence, Volume).
Synonyms, alternate names, or legacy names for this observation. Supports search and mapping from legacy systems.
The scale of measurement for the observation result. Qn=Quantitative (numeric), Ord=Ordinal (ranked), Nom=Nominal (named categories), Nar=Narrative (free text), Doc=Document (attached file).
An abbreviated display name for the LOINC code, used when space is limited in user interfaces or reports.
The source instrument or questionnaire from which the survey question originates (e.g., PHQ-9, PROMIS, CAHPS).
For LOINC codes representing survey or assessment questions, this field contains the full question text as presented to the patient or clinician.
The specimen or body system from which the observation was made (e.g., Blood, Serum, Urine, Plasma, Cerebrospinal fluid).
The time dimension of the measurement (e.g., Point in time, 24 hour, 8 hour). Indicates whether the observation is a single point measurement or collected over a time interval.
The date and time when this LOINC code record was last modified. Audit trail field.
Primary key for major_diagnostic_category
Self-referencing FK on major_diagnostic_category (parent_major_diagnostic_category_id)
National average length of stay in days for cases grouped to this MDC. Used for benchmarking and utilization management.
Primary anatomical body system or organ system associated with this MDC (e.g., 'Cardiovascular', 'Respiratory', 'Musculoskeletal').
National ranking of this MDC by case volume (1 = highest volume). Used for prioritization and resource planning.
Type of classification logic used for this MDC: organ_system (anatomical), procedure_based (surgical/procedural), condition_based (disease-focused), or special_category (pre-MDC, ungroupable).
Additional clinical context, coding guidance, or special considerations for this MDC. Used by HIM and coding staff.
Type of CC/MCC logic applied within this MDC: standard (uses CC/MCC lists), modified (custom logic), or not_applicable (no CC partitioning).
Total number of DRGs contained within this MDC. Used for reference and validation.
Date when this MDC definition became effective for use in DRG grouping and reimbursement.
Federal fiscal year for which this MDC definition applies (e.g., 2024). CMS updates MDC definitions annually.
Ending ICD-10-CM diagnosis code that maps to this MDC (e.g., 'G99'). Used for grouper logic.
Starting ICD-10-CM diagnosis code that maps to this MDC (e.g., 'G00'). Used for grouper logic.
Ending ICD-10-PCS procedure code that maps to this MDC. Used for surgical partition assignment.
Starting ICD-10-PCS procedure code that maps to this MDC. Used for surgical partition assignment.
Indicates whether this MDC is currently active and available for use in DRG grouping. False for historical or deprecated MDCs.
Date when this MDC record was last modified in the reference data system. Used for change tracking and audit.
Detailed clinical and administrative description of the MDC scope, including typical diagnoses, procedures, and patient populations covered.
Full descriptive name of the major diagnostic category (e.g., 'Diseases and Disorders of the Nervous System').
Current lifecycle status of this MDC in the reference system. Active MDCs are used in current grouper logic.
Standard MDC code used in DRG grouping (e.g., MDC01, MDC02). This is the externally-known unique identifier for the category.
Numeric representation of the MDC (1-25). Used for sorting and grouping logic.
Indicates whether this is a pre-MDC assignment (e.g., transplants, tracheostomy, ECMO) that bypasses standard MDC logic. True for special high-resource cases.
Relative financial impact of this MDC on hospital reimbursement: high (high-cost, high-volume), medium, or low.
Average relative weight of all DRGs within this MDC. Used for cost and resource intensity analysis.
Abbreviated name for display and reporting purposes (e.g., 'Nervous System').
Indicates whether this MDC contains surgical DRGs, medical DRGs, or both. Not applicable for pre-MDC categories.
Date when this MDC definition was retired or superseded. Null for currently active MDCs.
Indicates whether this MDC represents ungroupable cases that do not fit standard classification logic. True for error DRGs.
Version identifier for this MDC definition (e.g., 'FY2024', 'v41.0'). Tracks annual updates to grouper logic.
Unique identifier for the NDC drug product record in the enterprise data warehouse.

Foreign key linking to reference.code_set_version. Business justification: NDC drug products are maintained by the FDA with weekly updates to the NDC Directory. The ndc_drug table has ndc_status attribute and marketing_start_date/marketing_end_date that track product lifecyc
The chemical substance or compound responsible for the therapeutic effect of the drug.
reference: FDA National Drug Code Directory, UNII

description: The FDA application number associated with the drug approval (e.g., NDA number, ANDA number, BLA number).
The WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification code, used internationally for drug classification.
reference: WHO Collaborating Centre for Drug Statistics Methodology

description: Indicates whether the drug is a biosimilar product, highly similar to an already-approved biological product.
Indicates whether the drug carries an FDA black box warning, the strictest warning for serious or life-threatening risks.
The controlled substance schedule classification assigned by the DEA (CI through CV), indicating the drug's potential for abuse and accepted medical use. Empty if not a controlled substance.
The physical form in which the drug is administered (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection, solution, cream, inhaler).
The date on which this NDC drug record became effective in the enterprise reference data system.
The date on which this NDC drug record is no longer valid or was superseded. Null if currently active.

business_glossary_term: Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) Medication Code
description: The standardized medication code used in FHIR MedicationRequest and Medication resources for interoperability.
Indicates whether the drug is included in the organization's formulary and any restrictions or preferences applied.
The Medi-Span Generic Product Identifier, a 14-character hierarchical classification code used in pharmacy systems.
Indicates whether the drug is classified as a high-alert medication by ISMP, requiring special handling and verification procedures.
The name of the company or entity that manufactures, repackages, or distributes the drug product.
The regulatory pathway under which the drug was approved (e.g., NDA, ANDA, BLA, OTC Monograph).
The date on which the drug product was discontinued or withdrawn from the market. Null if still active.
The date on which the drug product was first marketed or made available for distribution.
The 11-digit National Drug Code assigned by the FDA, uniquely identifying the labeler, product, and package size. Format: 5-4-2 (labeler-product-package).
The generic or non-proprietary name of the drug, typically the active ingredient name established by the United States Adopted Names (USAN) Council.
reference: FDA National Drug Code Directory, USAN

description: The therapeutic equivalence code from the FDA Orange Book, indicating whether a generic drug is therapeutically equivalent to the brand-name drug.
Indicates whether the drug is available for purchase without a prescription.
A textual description of the package size and configuration (e.g., bottle of 100 tablets, box of 10 vials).
The numeric quantity of units contained in the package.
The unit of measure for the package quantity (e.g., tablet, capsule, mL, vial).
The FDA pregnancy category classification indicating the risk of fetal harm (A=safest, X=contraindicated, N=not classified). Note: FDA replaced this with narrative labeling in 2015.
reference: FDA Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule

description: The full product name as registered with the FDA, including strength and dosage form.
The brand or trade name under which the drug is marketed to consumers and healthcare providers.
The timestamp when this NDC drug record was first created in the enterprise data warehouse.
The timestamp when this NDC drug record was last updated in the enterprise data warehouse.
Indicates whether the drug requires refrigerated storage to maintain stability and efficacy.
The path by which the drug is administered into the body (e.g., oral, intravenous, topical, subcutaneous, intramuscular).
reference: FDA National Drug Code Directory, HL7 FHIR RouteOfAdministration

description: The RxNorm Concept Unique Identifier assigned by the National Library of Medicine, providing a normalized drug concept mapping for interoperability.
The normalized drug name as defined in RxNorm, representing the clinical drug concept.
The source vocabulary from which the RxNorm concept was derived (e.g., RXNORM, VANDF, MMSL, NDDF).
Indicates whether the RxNorm concept is suppressed from use (N=not suppressed, Y=suppressed, O=obsolete, E=entry term).
The RxNorm term type classification (e.g., IN for ingredient, BN for brand name, SCD for semantic clinical drug, GPCK for generic pack).

business_glossary_term: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT) Code
description: The SNOMED CT concept code representing the drug product or substance for clinical documentation and interoperability.
The concentration or potency of the active ingredient(s) in the drug product, expressed as a numeric value with unit (e.g., 500 mg, 10 mg/mL).
The unit of measure for the drug strength (e.g., mg, mL, mcg, IU, %).
reference: FDA National Drug Code Directory, UCUM

description: The therapeutic or pharmacological classification of the drug (e.g., antibiotic, antihypertensive, analgesic).
reference: AHFS Drug Information, VA Drug Class

description: The FDA Unique Ingredient Identifier code for the active ingredient, used for substance identification.
Indicates whether the drug product is a vaccine used for immunization.

business_glossary_term: SNOMED CT (Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms) Concept Identifier
description: Unique identifier for the SNOMED CT concept as assigned by SNOMED International. This is the primary key and corresponds to the SCTID (SNOMED CT Identifier) in the SNOMED CT release files.
reference: SNOMED International SNOMED CT Release Format

description: The SNOMED CT release version identifier from which this concept was loaded (e.g., '20230901', '2023-09-01'). Supports version tracking and change management across SNOMED CT releases.
reference: SNOMED International SNOMED CT Release Notes

description: Identifier of the immediate parent concept in the SNOMED CT IS-A hierarchy. Used to navigate the taxonomy and determine subsumption relationships. A concept may have multiple parents in a polyhierarchy.
reference: SNOMED International SNOMED CT Concept Model

description: The typical section(s) of clinical documentation where this concept is used (e.g., 'Problem List', 'Allergies', 'Past Medical History', 'Assessment', 'Plan', 'Procedures'). Supports context-aware search and documentation templates.
reference: HL7 Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture (C-CDA) Implementation Guide

description: Additional classification of the concept beyond the semantic tag, used for grouping and filtering (e.g., 'diagnosis', 'symptom', 'surgical procedure', 'medication', 'laboratory test'). May be derived from semantic tag or additional metadata.
reference: SNOMED International SNOMED CT Editorial Guide

description: A formal textual definition of the concept providing clinical context and meaning. May be sourced from SNOMED International or supplemented with organizational definitions for clarity.

Current lifecycle status of the SNOMED CT concept. Active concepts are available for use in clinical documentation; inactive concepts are deprecated and should not be used for new entries but may appear in historical data.
reference: SNOMED International SNOMED CT Editorial Guide

business_glossary_term: CPT (Current Procedural Terminology) Map Target Code
description: The CPT code(s) to which this SNOMED CT procedure concept is mapped, if applicable. Supports billing and revenue cycle management by linking clinical procedures to reimbursable CPT codes.
reference: American Medical Association (AMA) CPT to SNOMED CT Map

description: The timestamp when this concept record was first created in the enterprise data platform. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this employer group's health plan is subject to ERISA federal regulations. True for most private employer plans. False for government and church plans which are ERISA-exempt.
reference: ERISA Title I, DOL ERISA Exemptions

description: The financial arrangement model for how the employer group funds its health benefits. Fully insured: payer assumes all risk. Self-funded: employer assumes claims risk. Level-funded: hybrid with predictable monthly payments. Minimum premium: employer funds expected claims, payer covers excess. Stop-loss only: employer self-funds with catastrophic reinsurance.
reference: ERISA Section 3, State Insurance Regulations, Self-Funded Plan Administration Standards

description: The number of days after the premium due date during which the employer group can make payment without coverage lapsing. Typically 30 days for group coverage. During the grace period, coverage remains active but claims may be pended.
reference: State Insurance Grace Period Requirements, ERISA Plan Document Standards

description: The legal or doing-business-as name of the employer organization that sponsors the health insurance coverage for its employees. This is the primary human-readable identifier for the group.

The externally-known unique business identifier assigned to the employer group by the payer. This is the group number printed on member ID cards and used in all billing and claims transactions. Also known as the policy group number or contract group number.
reference: HIPAA 834 Benefit Enrollment and Maintenance, X12 Standard

description: The total number of enrolled lives (employees and dependents) covered under this employer group. This count determines small group vs. large group classification for regulatory purposes and impacts premium rating methodologies.
reference: ACA Small Group Market Definition (under 50 employees), State Insurance Regulations

description: The current lifecycle status of the employer group contract. Active: coverage in force. Pending: application submitted, not yet effective. Suspended: temporarily inactive, may be reinstated. Terminated: contract ended by mutual agreement. Cancelled: contract ended by payer. Lapsed: contract ended due to non-payment.
reference: State Insurance Contract Law, ERISA Plan Termination Rules

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this employer group's benefit plan is HSA-qualified (high deductible health plan meeting IRS requirements). If true, employees can contribute pre-tax dollars to a Health Savings Account.
reference: IRS Publication 969 (Health Savings Accounts), IRC Section 223

description: The risk classification based on the employer's industry and occupation mix. Used in underwriting and premium rating. Low: office/professional. Moderate: light manufacturing/retail. High: construction/transportation. Hazardous: mining/heavy industrial.
reference: Occupational Risk Classification Standards, Workers Compensation Industry Codes

description: The minimum percentage of eligible employees that must enroll in the health plan for the group to qualify for coverage. Typically 75% for small groups. Used during initial underwriting and at renewal to prevent adverse selection.
reference: State Small Group Insurance Regulations, Underwriting Standards

business_glossary_term: North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code
description: The six-digit NAICS code that classifies the employer's industry sector. NAICS has largely replaced SIC for statistical and regulatory purposes. Used for industry analysis, risk stratification, and regulatory reporting.
The method by which the employer group remits premium payments to the payer. ACH and wire transfer are most common for large groups. Check and credit card may be used by small groups.
reference: Premium Payment Processing Standards, PCI DSS

description: The category of organization that sponsors the health plan. Private employer: for-profit or non-profit business. Union trust: labor union-sponsored plan. Government employer: federal, state, or local government entity. Association: group of small employers. Taft-Hartley: jointly trusteed union-management plan. MEWA: Multiple Employer Welfare Arrangement.
reference: ERISA Title I, Taft-Hartley Act Section 302(c)(5), DOL MEWA Regulations

description: The ZIP code or ZIP+4 code of the employer group's primary business address. Used for geographic rating, network assignment, and premium calculations. Format: XXXXX or XXXXX-XXXX.

The number of months for which the premium rates are guaranteed not to increase. Typically 12 months (annual rate guarantee) for most groups. Some large groups may negotiate multi-year rate guarantees.
reference: Insurance Contract Terms, Rate Guarantee Provisions

description: The annual date on which the employer group's contract renews. Typically the anniversary of the original effective date. Used for renewal underwriting, rate adjustments, and plan design changes.
reference: Insurance Contract Renewal Standards, ACA Rate Review Requirements

description: The four-digit Standard Industrial Classification code that categorizes the employer's primary line of business or industry. Used for risk assessment, underwriting, and industry benchmarking.
reference: U.S. Department of Labor SIC Manual

description: The state code that determines which state insurance regulations apply to this employer group. For fully insured plans, this is typically the state where the policy is issued. For self-funded ERISA plans, this may differ from the employer's physical location. Format: two uppercase letters.
reference: ERISA Preemption Rules, State Insurance Situs Regulations

description: The two-letter state abbreviation of the employer group's primary business address. Determines state insurance regulations, mandated benefits, and tax jurisdiction. Format: two uppercase letters (e.g., CA, NY, TX).
reference: USPS State Abbreviations, NAIC State Insurance Regulations

description: The date on which the employer group's coverage ends. Null if the group is currently active. Once set, no new claims with service dates after this date will be paid under this group.
reference: ERISA Plan Termination Rules, COBRA Continuation Coverage Requirements

description: The risk classification assigned to this employer group during underwriting. Standard: average risk. Preferred: lower than average risk, may receive rate discounts. Substandard: higher than average risk, may have rate loadings or exclusions. Declined: group was not accepted for coverage.
reference: NAIC Model Regulation for Group Health Insurance, Underwriting Standards

description: The date and time when this employer group record was last modified. Updated whenever any attribute changes. Used for change tracking and data synchronization. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: Data Governance Standards, Change Data Capture Standards

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this employer group has an active wellness or health promotion program integrated with their health plan. Wellness programs may include biometric screenings, health risk assessments, smoking cessation, weight management, and premium incentives.
reference: ACA Wellness Program Regulations, HIPAA Wellness Program Rules

description: Unique identifier for the member enrollment record. Primary key for this transactional enrollment entity.
Unique identifier for the members assigned primary care physician. Required for HMO and POS plans.
Policy identifier assigned by the health insurance exchange for marketplace enrollments. Used for reconciliation with exchange data.

Unique identifier for the member (subscriber or dependent) enrolled in the health plan. Links to the member master record.
Unique identifier for the insurance payer or health plan organization providing coverage. Links to the payer master record.

Unique identifier for the provider network associated with this enrollment. Determines in-network vs out-of-network benefits.

Start date of the benefit period for deductible and out-of-pocket maximum tracking. Typically calendar year or plan year.

business_glossary_term: Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (COBRA) Indicator

Coverage tier indicating the scope of family members covered under this enrollment. Affects premium calculation.

Reason for enrollment termination. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: voluntary_disenrollment|employment_termination|loss_of_eligibility|non_payment|death|medicare_eligibility|medicaid_eligibility|plan_discontinuation|other — promote to reference product]
