business_glossary_term: Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (COBRA) Premium Amount
description: Premium amount charged to COBRA participants, typically 102% of the group rate to cover administrative costs. Null for non-COBRA billing. Expressed in USD.
Timestamp when this premium billing record was first created in the system.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this billing record. Typically USD for US-based healthcare payers.
Date on which this premium billing became delinquent due to non-payment past the due date. Null if payment is current or received.
Portion of the total premium paid by the employee or subscriber through payroll deduction or direct payment. Expressed in USD.
Portion of the total premium paid by the employer group on behalf of enrolled members. Zero for individual and COBRA billing. Expressed in USD.
Total number of covered members (subscriber plus dependents) enrolled under this billing arrangement during the billing period.
Last date of the grace period during which coverage remains active despite non-payment. After this date, coverage may lapse. Typically 30-90 days per plan terms.
Date on which this premium billing invoice was generated and issued to the responsible party.
Externally visible unique invoice number assigned to this premium billing statement for tracking and payment reconciliation.
Date on which the premium billing invoice was transmitted or mailed to the responsible party.
Date on which health plan coverage lapsed or was terminated due to non-payment of premium. Null if coverage remains active or payment was received.
Net premium amount due after applying all contributions, subsidies, and adjustments. This is the amount the responsible party must remit. Expressed in USD.

Remaining unpaid balance on this premium invoice after applying all payments. Zero indicates invoice is paid in full. Expressed in USD.
Total amount of premium payment received and applied to this invoice. May differ from net premium due in cases of partial payment or overpayment. Expressed in USD.
Method by which premium payment was received: ACH, wire transfer, check, credit card, payroll deduction, or electronic funds transfer.
Date on which premium payment was received and posted to the account. Null if payment has not been received.
External reference number or transaction identifier for the premium payment, such as check number, ACH trace number, or credit card authorization code.

business_glossary_term: Premium Rate Per Member Per Month (PMPM)
description: The per-member-per-month premium rate applied to calculate total premium for this billing period. Expressed in USD.
Indicates whether the lapsed coverage is eligible for reinstatement upon payment of outstanding premium and any applicable fees. True if reinstatement is allowed per plan terms.
Government subsidy or premium tax credit amount applied to reduce the net premium owed by the subscriber. Applicable to exchange plans. Expressed in USD.
reference: Affordable Care Act (ACA) Premium Tax Credit Rules (26 USC 36B)

description: Total premium amount billed for the coverage period before applying employer or subscriber contributions. Expressed in USD.
User identifier or system account that last updated this premium billing record.
Timestamp when this premium billing record was last modified or updated.

Unique identifier for the subscriber record. Primary key. The subscriber is the primary insured individual (policyholder) who holds the insurance contract with the payer and is responsible for premium payment.
Reference to the employer group sponsoring this coverage, if applicable. Null for individual/non-group plans.
Reference to the specific health plan product under which this subscriber is enrolled. Links to the plan master in the insurance domain.

Payer-assigned unique member identifier for the subscriber. This is the externally-known subscriber number used on insurance cards and in claims processing. Also known as subscriber number or policy number.
Reference to the insurance payer (health plan) that issued this subscriber contract. Links to the payer master in the insurance domain.

Primary street address line for the subscriber's residence.

business_glossary_term: Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (COBRA) Eligible Flag
description: Indicates whether the subscriber is eligible for COBRA continuation coverage after employment termination. True=eligible, False=not eligible.

business_glossary_term: Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (COBRA) End Date
description: Date when COBRA continuation coverage ends, if applicable. Null if not on COBRA or coverage is ongoing.

business_glossary_term: Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (COBRA) Start Date
description: Date when COBRA continuation coverage began, if applicable. Null if not on COBRA.
Three-letter ISO country code of the subscriber's residence. Typically USA for US-based subscribers.
Current lifecycle status of the subscriber's coverage. Active=currently covered, Inactive=coverage lapsed, Suspended=temporarily paused, Terminated=permanently ended, Pending=awaiting activation.
Type of insurance coverage provided under this subscriber contract. Indicates the primary benefit category.
Timestamp when this subscriber record was first created in the data platform.
Date of birth of the subscriber. Used for eligibility verification and age-based benefit determination.
Indicates whether the subscriber is dually eligible for both Medicare and Medicaid. True=dual eligible, False=not dual eligible. Critical for coordination of benefits and cost-sharing determination.

description: Date when the subscriber's coverage terminates. Null for open-ended active coverage.
Date when the subscriber's coverage becomes effective and benefits are available.

Legal last name (family name) of the subscriber as registered with the payer.
Indicates whether the subscriber is eligible for Medicaid coverage. True=eligible, False=not eligible. Used for coordination of benefits and dual eligibility determination.
State-issued Medicaid identification number, if the subscriber is Medicaid-eligible. Used for coordination of benefits.
Indicates whether the subscriber is eligible for Medicare coverage. True=eligible, False=not eligible. Used for coordination of benefits.
Medicare Beneficiary Identifier (MBI) assigned by CMS, if the subscriber is Medicare-eligible. Used for coordination of benefits between Medicare and commercial insurance.
Middle name or initial of the subscriber, if provided.
Network tier or level assigned to the subscriber's plan. Determines cost-sharing and provider access levels.

ZIP code or postal code of the subscriber's residence.

description: National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the subscriber's designated primary care physician, if applicable. Used in managed care plans requiring PCP assignment.

Relationship of the subscriber to the primary insured. For subscriber records, this is typically 'self' since the subscriber IS the insured party. Used when subscriber may be a dependent on another policy.

business_glossary_term: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Malpractice Payment Flag
description: Indicates whether the NPDB response contains one or more medical malpractice payment reports. True triggers mandatory committee review and documentation of the committee's assessment of the payment history.
reference: NPDB Guidebook; 45 CFR Part 60; NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 5

business_glossary_term: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Query Date
description: The date on which the NPDB query was submitted for this credentialing application. Must be within 180 days of the credentialing decision per NCQA standards.
reference: NPDB Guidebook; 45 CFR Part 60; NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 5

business_glossary_term: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Query Type
description: Type of NPDB query submitted: initial query at first credentialing, reappointment query at biennial renewal, or enrollment in the continuous query program for ongoing monitoring of adverse actions and malpractice payments.
reference: NPDB Guidebook; 45 CFR Part 60; NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 5; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

business_glossary_term: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Query Reference Number
description: The unique reference number assigned by the NPDB to the submitted query. Used for audit trail, regulatory reporting, and reconciliation with NPDB records.
reference: NPDB Guidebook; 45 CFR Part 60; NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 5

business_glossary_term: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Response Date
description: The date on which the NPDB response was received for the submitted query. Used to confirm timely receipt and to calculate query-to-response turnaround.
reference: NPDB Guidebook; 45 CFR Part 60; NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 5

business_glossary_term: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Response Status
description: Outcome of the NPDB query: no_report indicates a clean response with no adverse action or malpractice payment reports; report_found indicates one or more reports exist requiring committee review.
reference: NPDB Guidebook; 45 CFR Part 60; NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 5

description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier assigned to the clinician by CMS. Required on all credentialing applications and used for payer enrollment, claims processing, and provider directory maintenance.
reference: CMS NPI Final Rule 45 CFR Part 162; HIPAA Administrative Simplification

business_glossary_term: Office of Inspector General (OIG) Exclusion Check Status
description: Result of the OIG List of Excluded Individuals and Entities (LEIE) screening to confirm the provider is not excluded from participation in federal healthcare programs (Medicare, Medicaid). Must be checked at initial credentialing and at least monthly thereafter.
reference: OIG LEIE; 42 USC §1320a-7; CMS Conditions of Participation; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: The number of peer reference evaluations collected for this credentialing application. NCQA and Joint Commission standards typically require a minimum of three peer references from physicians familiar with the applicant's clinical competency.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 7; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

description: Indicates whether the required minimum number of peer reference evaluations have been received and reviewed for this application. True when all required references are on file and meet quality standards.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 7; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

description: Status of the formal peer review summary evaluation completed for the reappointment cycle, assessing clinical performance, professional conduct, and adherence to evidence-based practice standards. Protected under state peer review statutes.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 8; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.07; HCQIA; State Peer Review Protection Statutes

description: The date on which any granted provisional clinical privileges expire. Provisional privileges must be converted to full privileges or terminated upon completion of the credentialing review.
reference: The Joint Commission MS.06.01.05; CMS Conditions of Participation 42 CFR §482.22

description: Indicates whether provisional (temporary) clinical privileges have been granted to the provider pending completion of the full credentialing review. Provisional privileges are time-limited and require a supervising physician attestation.
reference: The Joint Commission MS.06.01.05; CMS Conditions of Participation 42 CFR §482.22

business_glossary_term: Primary Source Verification (PSV) Education and Training Status
description: Status of primary source verification of the provider's medical education (medical school graduation) and graduate medical education (residency/fellowship) directly with the issuing institutions or through ECFMG for international graduates.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 4; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; ECFMG (Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates)

description: Status of primary source verification of the provider's state medical license directly with the issuing state medical board. A core PSV element required by NCQA and Joint Commission credentialing standards.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 4; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; FSMB (Federation of State Medical Boards)

business_glossary_term: Primary Source Verification (PSV) Work History Status
description: Status of verification of the provider's five-year work history, including gaps in employment or training exceeding six months, as required by NCQA credentialing standards.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 4; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

description: Status of the review of clinical quality indicators (e.g., outcomes data, complication rates, mortality rates, HEDIS measures) for the reappointment period. Populated for reappointment and privilege expansion applications.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 8; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.07; CMS MIPS/APM Quality Reporting

description: The end date of the clinical performance review period evaluated during a reappointment credentialing cycle. Marks the close of the 24-month interval used to assess quality indicators and peer review summaries.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 8; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.07

description: The start date of the clinical performance review period evaluated during a reappointment credentialing cycle. Captures the beginning of the 24-month interval of quality indicators, peer review summaries, and CME compliance assessed for reappointment.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 8; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.07; CMS Conditions of Participation

description: The date the medical staff office officially received and logged the credentialing application. May differ from submission_date when applications are mailed or submitted through intermediaries such as CAQH ProView.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 1; CAQH ProView

business_glossary_term: System for Award Management (SAM) Exclusion Check Status
description: Result of the SAM.gov federal exclusion database screening confirming the provider is not debarred or suspended from federal programs. Required in addition to OIG LEIE screening for comprehensive exclusion verification.
reference: SAM.gov; FAR 52.209-6; OIG Compliance Program Guidance; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: The provider's secondary or subspecialty clinical area for which additional privileges may be requested (e.g., Interventional Cardiology as a subspecialty of Cardiology). Nullable when no secondary specialty applies.
reference: American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS); NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 4

description: The date on which the clinician formally submitted the completed credentialing application to the medical staff office. Serves as the principal business event date for the credentialing lifecycle and is used to calculate processing turnaround time.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 1; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.01

description: Indicates whether the provider has obtained tail coverage (extended reporting endorsement) for a prior claims-made policy. Required when a provider transitions between employers or facilities to ensure coverage for claims arising from prior practice.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 6; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

description: Indicates whether the provider is requesting telemedicine or telehealth clinical privileges as part of this credentialing application. Telemedicine credentialing may follow an expedited pathway per CMS and Joint Commission standards.
reference: The Joint Commission MS.06.01.05; CMS Telemedicine Credentialing and Privileging Final Rule 42 CFR §482.12; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: The timestamp when the credentialing application record was most recently modified in the system. Used for change tracking, ETL delta processing, and audit trail compliance.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b) Audit Controls; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF

description: Primary key for credentialing_file
Reference to the hospital, clinic, or healthcare facility where the provider is seeking privileges or credentialing.
Reference to the credentialing committee or review body responsible for evaluating this application.
Reference to the staff member or committee member assigned as the primary reviewer for this credentialing file.
Reference to the insurance payer or health plan for which the provider is seeking network enrollment, if applicable.
Self-referencing FK on credentialing_file (prior_credentialing_file_id)

Foreign key linking to provider.clinician. Business justification: Credentialing files are maintained for individual clinicians (the provider being credentialed). The credentialing_file table has a generic provider_id which should be normalized to provider_clinician_
Date when the provider filed a formal appeal of the credentialing decision.
Indicates whether the provider has filed a formal appeal of the credentialing decision.
Result of the provider's appeal of the credentialing decision.
Date when the credentialing application was formally submitted for review. Represents the principal business event timestamp for this credentialing file.
Indicates whether a comprehensive background check, including criminal history and sanctions screening, has been completed for the provider.
Date when the background check was completed.
Indicates whether the provider's board certification status has been verified with the relevant specialty board.
Date when the provider last attested to the accuracy of their CAQH ProView profile, if applicable.
Unique identifier assigned to the provider in the CAQH ProView system for centralized credentialing data management.
Any conditions, limitations, or restrictions placed on the provider's credentialing approval or clinical privileges.
Timestamp when this credentialing file record was first created in the system.
Current lifecycle status of the credentialing file indicating its position in the credentialing workflow.
Indicates whether the provider's DEA registration number has been verified with the Drug Enforcement Administration for controlled substance prescribing authority.
Final determination made by the credentialing committee or review body regarding the provider's application.
Detailed explanation and justification for the credentialing decision, including any conditions, restrictions, or reasons for denial.
Indicates whether the provider's medical education, training, and residency credentials have been verified with the issuing institutions.
Date when the credentialing approval becomes active and the provider is authorized to practice or participate in networks.
Date when the credentialing approval expires and requires renewal or reappointment.
Externally-known unique business identifier for the credentialing file, used for tracking and reference across systems and communications.
Classification of the credentialing file indicating the purpose and scope of the credentialing activity.
Indicates whether the provider's current and past hospital privileges have been verified with other healthcare facilities.
Indicates whether the provider's professional license has been verified with the appropriate state licensing board.
Total dollar amount of professional liability insurance coverage maintained by the provider.
Indicates whether the provider's professional liability (malpractice) insurance coverage has been verified and meets minimum requirements.
Additional notes, comments, or observations related to the credentialing file and review process.
Indicates whether the provider's National Provider Identifier has been verified against the National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES).
Indicates whether peer references from other healthcare professionals have been contacted and verified.
Detailed list or description of specific clinical privileges, procedures, or practice authorities the provider is requesting.
Number of months between credentialing cycles for this provider, typically 24 or 36 months per regulatory requirements.
Date when the credentialing review process was completed and a decision was rendered.
Date when the credentialing committee or review body began formal evaluation of the application.
Indicates whether screening against federal and state exclusion lists (OIG, SAM, state Medicaid exclusions) has been completed.
Date when sanctions screening was completed.
Primary medical specialty or clinical area for which the provider is seeking credentialing or privileges.
Username or identifier of the system user who last modified this credentialing file record.
Timestamp when this credentialing file record was last modified in the system.
Username or identifier of the system user who created this credentialing file record.
Unique surrogate identifier for each DEA controlled substance registration record in the enterprise data platform. Primary key for the dea_registration data product.

Reference to the primary healthcare facility or practice location associated with this DEA registration. DEA registrations are location-specific; this links the registration to the enterprise facility master record for network and compliance reporting.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.12; Joint Commission Credentialing Standards

description: Reference to the licensed healthcare professional or organizational provider who holds this DEA registration. Links to the authoritative provider master record.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301; NPI Registry — CMS

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_submission. Business justification: DEA registration renewals and modifications are regulatory submissions to DEA. Credentialing teams track submission dates, DEA confirmation numbers, payment receipts, and approval status to maintain u

Reference to the provider's credentialing record in the credentialing management system (e.g., Symplr). Links the DEA registration to the broader credentialing and privileging workflow for the provider.
reference: Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; NCQA Credentialing Standards; Symplr Credentialing

description: The DEA-defined category of business activity for which the registration is issued. Determines the type of controlled substance activities the registrant is authorized to perform. Practitioner covers physicians, dentists, and veterinarians; mid-level practitioner covers nurse practitioners and physician assistants; hospital and pharmacy cover institutional registrants. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: practitioner|mid-level_practitioner|hospital|pharmacy|researcher|manufacturer|distributor|importer|exporter|reverse_distributor|narcotic_treatment_program — promote to reference product]
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.13; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: The number of calendar days remaining until the DEA registration expires, calculated as of the most recent data refresh date. Supports proactive credentialing management and pharmacy compliance dashboards. Note: This is a point-in-time snapshot value loaded during ETL; it is not a real-time computed field.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.31; Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

description: The official DEA registration number assigned by the Drug Enforcement Administration to authorize the registrant to handle controlled substances. Format: two-letter prefix followed by seven digits. Used for pharmacy order validation and controlled substance prescribing verification.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.13; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: The date on which the expiration alert notification was sent to the provider and/or credentialing staff. Null if no alert has been sent. Used for credentialing workflow audit trails.
reference: Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; Internal Credentialing Policy

description: Indicates whether an expiration alert notification has been sent to the provider and/or credentialing staff regarding the upcoming expiration of this DEA registration. Supports proactive renewal workflow management.
reference: Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; Internal Credentialing Policy

description: The calendar date on which the DEA registration expires and the provider is no longer authorized to prescribe or handle controlled substances under this registration. DEA registrations are typically issued for a three-year term. Critical for pharmacy order validation and compliance monitoring.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.13; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: The registration fee paid to the DEA for the current registration period, in U.S. dollars. DEA registration fees vary by registrant type and are set by federal regulation. Used for credentialing cost tracking and budget reconciliation.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.21; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: Indicates whether the registrant is exempt from DEA registration fees. Fee exemptions apply to federal, state, and local government practitioners, as well as certain public health service providers. Relevant for registration cost tracking and compliance.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.21; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: Free-text field for credentialing staff to document additional context, exceptions, or administrative notes related to the DEA registration. Examples include documentation of DEA correspondence, special conditions, or manual verification notes.
reference: Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; Internal Credentialing Policy

description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) associated with the provider holding this DEA registration. Used to cross-reference the DEA registration with the provider's NPI record for pharmacy claims validation, payer enrollment verification, and PDMP (Prescription Drug Monitoring Program) reporting.
reference: CMS NPI Registry; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 162.406; Health Level Seven (HL7) FHIR Practitioner Resource

description: The date on which the DEA registration fee was paid for the current registration period. Used for financial reconciliation and credentialing audit trails.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.21; DEA Diversion Control Division

business_glossary_term: Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) Reporting Required Flag
description: Indicates whether the provider holding this DEA registration is subject to mandatory Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) reporting requirements in the registered state. PDMP reporting obligations vary by state and practitioner type.
reference: State PDMP Statutes; PDMP TTAC (Training and Technical Assistance Center); DEA Diversion Control Division

description: DEA-assigned code identifying the specific practitioner type category (e.g., MD, DO, DDS, DVM, NP, PA, CRNA). Determines prescribing authority scope and schedule authorization eligibility. Sourced from DEA registration application form. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MD|DO|DDS|DMD|DVM|NP|PA|CRNA|CNM|PharmD|RPh|ND|OD|DPM|PhD — promote to reference product]
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1300.01; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: The timestamp when this DEA registration record was first created in the enterprise data platform. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and compliance reporting requirements.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164.312; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001

description: The timestamp when this DEA registration record was most recently updated in the enterprise data platform. Used for change tracking, incremental ETL processing, and audit compliance.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164.312; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001

description: Primary street address line of the practice location registered with the DEA. The DEA registration is location-specific; a provider with multiple practice sites may require separate registrations per location.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.12; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: Secondary address line (suite, floor, unit number) of the practice location registered with the DEA. Supplements the primary address line for precise location identification.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.12; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: City of the practice location registered with the DEA for this controlled substance registration.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.12; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: The full legal name of the individual practitioner or organization as it appears on the DEA registration certificate. May differ from the provider's operational display name. Used for verification against DEA public registry and pharmacy dispensing records.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.13; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: U.S. ZIP or ZIP+4 postal code of the practice location registered with the DEA. Used for geographic analysis of controlled substance prescribing patterns and regulatory reporting.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.12; USPS Postal Standards

description: The calendar date on which the DEA registration was originally issued or most recently renewed by the Drug Enforcement Administration. Represents the effective start of the current registration period.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.13; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: The U.S. state or territory in which the DEA registration is valid and the provider is authorized to prescribe controlled substances. DEA registrations are state-specific; a provider practicing in multiple states requires a separate DEA registration for each state. Represented as a two-letter USPS state abbreviation.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.12; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: Current lifecycle status of the DEA registration. Active indicates the registration is valid and the provider may prescribe controlled substances. Expired indicates the registration has lapsed and must be renewed before prescribing. Suspended or revoked indicates regulatory action has been taken.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.36; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: Indicates whether the DEA registration is held by an individual practitioner or by an institutional entity (e.g., hospital, clinic, pharmacy). Institutional registrations cover all authorized practitioners operating under the institution's DEA number.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.12; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: The date on which the provider submitted a renewal application to the DEA for continuation of the controlled substance registration. DEA regulations require renewal applications to be submitted at least 45 days before expiration. Used for credentialing workflow tracking in Symplr.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.31; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: The confirmation or tracking number issued by the DEA upon receipt of a renewal application. Used to track the status of pending renewals and follow up with the DEA Diversion Control Division.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.31; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: The date on which the DEA registration was formally revoked by the Drug Enforcement Administration. Revocation is a permanent action distinct from suspension. Null when the registration has not been revoked.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.36; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: Indicates whether the DEA registration authorizes the provider to prescribe Schedule II controlled substances (e.g., opioids such as oxycodone, stimulants such as amphetamine). Schedule II substances have high abuse potential with severe psychological or physical dependence. Required for CPOE validation in Epic Willow and Cerner PharmNet.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308.12; Controlled Substances Act

description: Indicates whether the DEA registration authorizes the provider to prescribe Schedule III controlled substances (e.g., anabolic steroids, buprenorphine combinations). Schedule III substances have moderate to low physical dependence potential.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308.13; Controlled Substances Act

description: Indicates whether the DEA registration authorizes the provider to prescribe Schedule IIN non-narcotic controlled substances (e.g., stimulants such as methylphenidate, Adderall). Distinct from Schedule IIN narcotic authorizations for pharmacy dispensing and order validation purposes.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308.12; Controlled Substances Act

description: Indicates whether the DEA registration authorizes the provider to prescribe Schedule IV controlled substances (e.g., benzodiazepines, tramadol). Schedule IV substances have lower abuse potential relative to Schedule III.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308.14; Controlled Substances Act

description: Indicates whether the DEA registration authorizes the provider to prescribe Schedule V controlled substances (e.g., cough preparations with less than 200mg of codeine per 100mL). Schedule V substances have the lowest abuse potential among controlled substances.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308.15; Controlled Substances Act

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this DEA registration record was sourced or last updated. Supports data lineage tracking and ETL reconciliation across credentialing platforms.
reference: HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; Internal Data Governance Standards

description: The native record identifier for this DEA registration in the originating operational system (e.g., Symplr provider ID, Epic provider record number). Used for ETL reconciliation and cross-system traceability.
reference: HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; Internal Data Governance Standards

description: The date on which the provider voluntarily surrendered the DEA registration to the Drug Enforcement Administration. Voluntary surrender may occur upon retirement, change of practice, or in lieu of revocation proceedings.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.52; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: The date on which the DEA registration was suspended by the Drug Enforcement Administration or voluntarily surrendered by the provider. Null when the registration has not been suspended. Triggers immediate pharmacy order blocking in CPOE systems.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.36; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: Narrative description of the reason for suspension or revocation of the DEA registration, as documented by the DEA or the provider's credentialing department. Includes regulatory action codes, voluntary surrender reasons, or administrative hold explanations.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301.36; OIG Exclusion Database

description: The most recent date on which the DEA registration was verified against the DEA Diversion Control Division public registry or through a primary source verification process. Required for Joint Commission and NCQA credentialing compliance.
reference: Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; NCQA Credentialing Standards; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: The method used to verify the DEA registration during the credentialing or re-credentialing process. DEA portal indicates direct query to the DEA Diversion Control Division online registry; primary source indicates direct contact with the DEA; third party indicates use of a credentialing verification organization (CVO).
reference: Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; NCQA Credentialing Standards; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: Indicates whether the provider holds a DATA 2000 waiver (formerly X-waiver) authorizing the prescribing of buprenorphine for opioid use disorder treatment in an office-based setting. As of the SUPPORT Act (2023), the X-waiver requirement was eliminated, but this flag tracks historical and current waiver status for compliance and analytics.
reference: Drug Addiction Treatment Act of 2000 (DATA 2000); SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Act (2018); DEA 21 CFR Part 1301; SAMHSA

description: The maximum number of patients the provider is authorized to treat with buprenorphine for opioid use disorder under the DATA 2000 waiver. Common limits are 30, 100, or 275 patients depending on provider type and waiver tier. Null if x_waiver_authorized is false or not applicable.
reference: Drug Addiction Treatment Act of 2000 (DATA 2000); SAMHSA; DEA Diversion Control Division

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each education and training record associated with a healthcare provider. Serves as the primary key for this entity in the Silver Layer lakehouse.
Reference to the healthcare provider (physician, nurse, allied health professional) whose educational and training history this record documents. Links to the authoritative provider master record.
reference: Symplr Credentialing; NCQA Credentialing Standards; CMS Provider Enrollment

description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Training records for workforce employees pursuing or maintaining clinical roles. Real business need: competency verification, promotion eligibility, continuing education compliance, career development

Current accreditation standing of the educational institution or training program at the time of the provider's enrollment or completion. Probationary or withdrawn accreditation may affect credentialing eligibility.
reference: ACGME Institutional Requirements; NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

description: Name or code of the accrediting organization that has certified the educational institution or training program (e.g., ACGME for residency/fellowship, LCME for allopathic medical schools, COCA for osteopathic medical schools, CCNE for nursing programs). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ACGME|LCME|COCA|CCNE|ACEN|AOA|AAMC|ECFMG|CODA|ACPE|other — promote to reference product]
reference: ACGME Institutional Requirements; LCME Accreditation Standards; COCA Accreditation; NCQA Credentialing Standards

business_glossary_term: Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) Accredited Flag
description: Indicates whether the residency or fellowship training program is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME). ACGME accreditation is a key credentialing requirement for hospital privileges and payer enrollment.
reference: ACGME Institutional Requirements; NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

description: Date on which the provider successfully completed or graduated from the educational program, residency, fellowship, or training. Nullable if the program is currently in progress. Required for primary source verification.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; Symplr Credentialing

description: Type of credential document issued upon completion of the educational or training program. Distinguishes between formal degrees, certificates of completion, and program-specific credentials for credentialing file management.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; Symplr Credentialing

description: Degree, diploma, or certificate conferred upon successful completion of the educational program (e.g., MD, DO, PhD, DNP, RN, BSN). Required for credentialing primary source verification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MD|DO|PhD|DNP|NP|PA|RN|BSN|MSN|DDS|DMD|PharmD|DPM|DC|OD|MPH|MBA|Certificate — promote to reference product]
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; ACGME Program Requirements

description: Description of the discrepancy identified between the provider's self-reported educational information and the primary source verification result. Populated only when discrepancy_flag is true. Required for credentialing committee review documentation.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; OIG Compliance Guidance

description: Indicates whether a discrepancy was identified between the information provided by the provider on their credentialing application and the information confirmed through primary source verification. Triggers a credentialing review workflow.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; OIG Compliance Guidance

description: Indicates whether a copy of the degree certificate, diploma, or completion letter has been received and stored in the provider's credentialing file. Required for credentialing file completeness audits.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; Symplr Credentialing

description: Date on which the credential document (diploma, certificate, completion letter) was received and added to the provider's credentialing file. Supports credentialing file completeness tracking.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; Symplr Credentialing

business_glossary_term: Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG) Certificate Number
description: Unique certificate number issued by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG) to international medical graduates. Used for primary source verification of foreign medical education credentials.
reference: ECFMG Certification Requirements; NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

business_glossary_term: Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG) Certified Flag
description: Indicates whether the provider holds ECFMG certification, applicable to international medical graduates (IMGs) who completed medical school outside the United States or Canada. ECFMG certification is required for IMGs to enter ACGME-accredited residency programs.
reference: ECFMG Certification Requirements; ACGME Program Requirements; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: Four-digit calendar year in which the provider graduated or completed the program. Used for quick filtering and reporting in credentialing dashboards when exact completion date is not available.

Academic honors, distinctions, or awards received upon completion of the educational program (e.g., Alpha Omega Alpha Honor Medical Society, summa cum laude, chief resident designation). Captured for provider profile completeness.

Indicates whether the provider is an international medical graduate (IMG), meaning they completed their basic medical degree outside the United States or Canada. Drives ECFMG verification requirements and specific credentialing pathways.
reference: ECFMG Certification Requirements; ACGME Program Requirements; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: City where the educational institution or training program is located. Used for primary source verification and geographic reporting.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the country where the educational institution or training program is located. Required for international medical graduate (IMG) identification and ECFMG verification workflows.
reference: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; ECFMG Certification; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: Full legal name of the educational institution, medical school, residency program host hospital, fellowship program, or training organization where the provider completed their education or training (e.g., Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, Mayo Clinic Residency Program).
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; Symplr Credentialing

description: Two-letter US state abbreviation (or equivalent province/territory code) where the educational institution or training program is located. Used for licensure cross-referencing and credentialing workflows.

Indicates whether this is the current active version of the education and training record for the provider. Supports slowly changing dimension (SCD) management in the Silver Layer, where historical versions may be retained for audit purposes.

reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164

description: High-level classification of the credential record. Distinguishes among state medical/nursing licenses, DEA controlled substance registrations, specialty board certifications, and CME (Continuing Medical Education) activity completions. Drives downstream workflow routing in credentialing and privileging systems such as Symplr.
reference: Symplr Credentialing; NCQA Credentialing Standards; URAC Credentialing Standards

description: The number of days remaining until this credential expires, calculated from the current date to the expiration_date. Used for proactive renewal alerting and credentialing dashboard KPIs. Negative values indicate the credential is already expired.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

business_glossary_term: DEA (Drug Enforcement Administration) Business Activity Type
description: The DEA-designated business activity type associated with the DEA registration. Defines the authorized scope of controlled substance handling (e.g., practitioner prescribing vs. hospital dispensing vs. research). Applicable only to DEA registration credential types.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301; DEA Registration Application Form 224

description: Comma-separated list of controlled substance schedule authorizations granted under this DEA registration (e.g., 'II,III,IV,V'). Applicable only to DEA registration credential types. Used by pharmacy order validation systems (Epic Willow, Cerner PharmNet) to authorize controlled substance prescribing.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308; Controlled Substances Act; CMS Conditions of Participation

description: The date from which this credential record is considered effective and authorizes clinical practice or activity. For state licenses and DEA registrations, this aligns with the issue_date. For board certifications, this is the initial certification effective date. Supports temporal validity queries.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; FHIR Practitioner Resource

description: The date until which this credential record is considered effective. Aligns with expiration_date for most credential types. Null for open-ended or lifetime credentials. Supports SCD (Slowly Changing Dimension) and temporal validity queries in the lakehouse.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; FHIR Practitioner Resource

description: The date on which the credential expires and must be renewed or recertified to remain valid. Null for credentials with no expiration (e.g., certain lifetime board certifications). Drives automated renewal alerts in Symplr and Epic credentialing workflows.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; DEA 21 CFR Part 1301

description: The date on which the credential was originally issued or first conferred by the issuing authority. For board certifications, this is the initial certification date. For CME activities, this is the activity completion date.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; ABMS Board Certification Standards; ACCME Standards

description: Full name of the organization or governmental body that issued or confers this credential (e.g., 'Texas Medical Board', 'U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration', 'American Board of Internal Medicine', 'American Medical Association — PRA'). Used for primary source verification routing.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; DEA 21 CFR Part 1301

description: Two-letter US state or territory abbreviation where the credential was issued. Applicable to state medical licenses and DEA state-specific registrations. Null for federal DEA registrations, board certifications, and CME activities that are not state-specific.
reference: State Medical Practice Acts; DEA 21 CFR Part 1301; FSMB Interstate Medical Licensure Compact

description: Current status of the provider's compliance with the Maintenance of Certification (MOC) program requirements for this board certification. MOC compliance is required by many hospitals for privileging and by payers for network participation. Applicable only to board certification credential types.
reference: ABMS MOC Program Requirements; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: Free-text field for credentialing staff to document relevant context, exceptions, or special circumstances associated with this credential record (e.g., pending renewal documentation, board action history, conditional license restrictions). Not used for structured data.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

business_glossary_term: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Queried Flag
description: Indicates whether the National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) was queried as part of the credentialing verification process for this provider. NPDB queries are required by CMS and The Joint Commission for initial credentialing and re-credentialing.
reference: NPDB Regulations 45 CFR Part 60; CMS Conditions of Participation 42 CFR Part 482; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

business_glossary_term: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Query Date
description: The date on which the NPDB was queried for this provider's credentialing record. Required documentation for CMS and Joint Commission credentialing compliance audits.
reference: NPDB Regulations 45 CFR Part 60; CMS Conditions of Participation 42 CFR Part 482

business_glossary_term: Office of Inspector General (OIG) Exclusion Check Date
description: The most recent date on which the OIG LEIE (List of Excluded Individuals/Entities) was checked for this provider. CMS recommends monthly screening; documents compliance for RAC audits and OIG investigations.
reference: OIG LEIE; CMS Conditions of Participation; OIG Advisory Opinion 98-14

business_glossary_term: Office of Inspector General (OIG) Exclusion List Checked Flag
description: Indicates whether the OIG (Office of Inspector General) List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE) was checked for this provider as part of credentialing. OIG exclusion screening is required by CMS; employing an excluded provider can result in significant civil monetary penalties.
reference: OIG LEIE; CMS Conditions of Participation; OIG Advisory Opinion 98-14

description: Indicates whether this credential is required for or submitted as part of payer enrollment and network participation applications. True = credential is submitted to payers (e.g., state license, DEA, board certification); False = not required for payer enrollment.
reference: CMS Provider Enrollment 42 CFR Part 424; CAQH ProView Standards; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: Indicates whether this credential has been verified directly with the issuing authority (primary source verification). True = verified with issuing authority; False = not yet primary source verified. Required for NCQA and Joint Commission credentialing accreditation.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; CMS Conditions of Participation 42 CFR Part 482

description: Indicates whether this credential is directly relevant to the provider's hospital privileging determination. True = this credential is required or considered in the privileging decision; False = informational only (e.g., a CME activity not tied to a specific privilege).
reference: The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; CMS Conditions of Participation 42 CFR Part 482.12

description: The date on which primary source verification was completed for this credential. NCQA and The Joint Commission require re-verification at defined intervals (typically every 3 years). Drives re-verification scheduling in Symplr.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; URAC Credentialing Standards

description: The method used to conduct primary source verification of this credential (e.g., online query to state medical board database, written confirmation from issuing authority, electronic query via NPDB or OIG). Documents the verification audit trail for accreditation surveys.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; NPDB Data Bank Regulations

description: The date by which the provider must complete recredentialing for this credential to maintain active status. NCQA and The Joint Commission require recredentialing at least every 3 years. Drives workflow queues in Symplr and credentialing management systems.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; CMS Conditions of Participation 42 CFR Part 482

description: The date on which the credential was most recently renewed or recertified by the issuing authority. Tracks the renewal history cycle for compliance reporting and credentialing re-verification workflows.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; State Medical Practice Acts; ABMS MOC Program

description: Description of any restrictions, conditions, or limitations placed on this credential by the issuing authority (e.g., 'Supervised practice only', 'No DEA Schedule II prescribing', 'Probationary license'). Null if no restrictions apply.
reference: State Medical Practice Acts; DEA 21 CFR Part 1301; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03

business_glossary_term: System for Award Management (SAM) Exclusion Checked Flag
description: Indicates whether the SAM.gov federal exclusions database was checked for this provider. SAM exclusion screening is required for providers participating in federal healthcare programs (Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP).

description: The native identifier of this credential record in the originating operational system of record (e.g., Symplr credential record ID, Epic provider record ID). Enables traceability from the lakehouse silver layer back to the source system for reconciliation and audit.

description: Granular classification within the credential type. For state licenses: MD, DO, RN, NP, PA, CRNA, PharmD, etc. For DEA registrations: Schedule II, III, IV, V authorization. reference: AMA CPT; DEA 21 CFR Part 1308; ABMS Board Certification Standards; AMA PRA Category 1

reference: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; SOC 2

description: Indicates the source used to verify this credential. Primary source verification (PSV) is required by NCQA, The Joint Commission, and CMS for credentialing. Secondary source verification uses intermediary databases. Self-reported credentials have not been independently verified.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; CMS Conditions of Participation 42 CFR Part 482

The date on which the provider formally filed an appeal or administrative challenge against the sanction. Null if no appeal has been filed. Used to track appeal timelines and statutory deadlines.

description: Indicates whether the sanctioned provider has filed a formal appeal or administrative challenge against the adverse action. A True value triggers additional workflow steps including legal review, credentialing committee notification, and potential temporary reinstatement consideration.
reference: NPDB; OIG Exclusion Program; Administrative Procedure Act

description: The result of the provider's formal appeal of the sanction. Upheld means the original sanction stands; overturned means the sanction was rescinded; modified means the terms were changed; withdrawn means the provider withdrew the appeal. Null if no appeal was filed or outcome is not yet determined.
reference: NPDB; OIG Exclusion Program; Administrative Procedure Act

description: Externally assigned case or docket number issued by the sanctioning authority (e.g., OIG case number, state medical board docket, DEA order number). Used for cross-referencing with the issuing regulatory body and NPDB reports.
reference: OIG Exclusion Program; NPDB (National Practitioner Data Bank); DEA

description: The OIG-assigned reference number for the Corporate Integrity Agreement associated with this sanction record. Null if no CIA was executed. Used for cross-referencing OIG CIA monitoring reports and compliance tracking.

The dollar amount of any civil monetary penalty assessed against the provider as part of or in conjunction with the sanction. Applicable when the OIG or CMS imposes financial penalties under the Civil Monetary Penalties Law. Zero or null if no monetary penalty was assessed.
reference: Civil Monetary Penalties Law 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7a; OIG; CMS

description: Indicates whether a Corporate Integrity Agreement was executed between the provider or organization and the OIG as a condition of reinstatement or settlement. A True value requires ongoing compliance monitoring, annual reporting, and independent review organization (IRO) oversight.
reference: OIG Corporate Integrity Agreement Program; False Claims Act 31 U.S.C. § 3729

description: The date and time when the sanction record was first created in the system. Serves as the audit trail anchor for record provenance, compliance documentation, and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF

description: Indicates whether a credentialing hold has been placed on the provider as a result of this sanction, preventing the granting or renewal of hospital privileges, payer enrollment, or network participation. True triggers automated workflow in the credentialing system (Symplr) to suspend privilege processing.
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) Medical Staff Standards; Symplr Credentialing; CMS Conditions of Participation

description: The DEA registration number of the provider at the time of the sanction, captured when the adverse action involves controlled substance violations or DEA revocation/suspension. Stored on the sanction record to preserve the identifier as of the action date.

OIG-specific exclusion classification code indicating whether the exclusion is mandatory (e.g., 1128(a)) or permissive (e.g., 1128(b)) under the Social Security Act. Mandatory exclusions require immediate termination from all federal healthcare programs; permissive exclusions are discretionary. Critical for CMS Conditions of Participation compliance.
reference: OIG Exclusion Program; Social Security Act § 1128; CMS Conditions of Participation

description: The scheduled end date of a time-limited sanction or probationary period as defined in the issuing authority's order. Distinct from reinstatement_date, which reflects actual restoration. Null for indefinite or permanent exclusions.
reference: OIG Exclusion Program; State Medical Board Standards; DEA

description: Indicates whether the sanction constitutes an exclusion from participation in federal healthcare programs including Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP, and other CMS-administered programs. True triggers mandatory termination of billing privileges and employment restrictions under CMS Conditions of Participation.
reference: OIG Exclusion Program; CMS Conditions of Participation; Social Security Act § 1128

description: The date on which the organization's credentialing committee, medical staff office, or compliance department completed its internal review of the sanction. Used to demonstrate timely response to adverse actions per TJC and CMS standards.
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) Medical Staff Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation

description: Current status of the organization's internal credentialing committee or compliance review of the sanction. Pending indicates review not yet initiated; in_review indicates active committee review; completed indicates review concluded; escalated indicates referral to senior leadership or legal counsel.
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) Medical Staff Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation; OIG Compliance Program Guidance

description: Name of the regulatory body, government agency, or licensing board that imposed the sanction (e.g., Office of Inspector General, Drug Enforcement Administration, State Medical Board of California, CMS, NPDB). Critical for determining the scope and legal basis of the adverse action.
reference: OIG Exclusion Program; DEA; CMS; State Departments of Health; NPDB

description: Categorical classification of the sanctioning authority level. Distinguishes federal exclusions (OIG, CMS, DEA) from state-level actions (state medical boards, state health departments) and accreditation bodies (The Joint Commission). Determines mandatory reporting and screening frequency requirements.
reference: OIG Exclusion Program; CMS Conditions of Participation; State Departments of Health

description: The state professional license number of the provider subject to the sanction at the time of the adverse action. Captured to preserve the license identifier as of the sanction date, particularly for state medical board revocations and suspensions.
reference: State Departments of Health; State Medical Board Standards; Symplr Credentialing

description: Two-letter US state abbreviation of the jurisdiction that issued the professional license affected by the sanction. Used to identify the applicable state medical board or licensing authority and to scope the geographic impact of the adverse action.
reference: State Departments of Health; State Medical Board Standards

description: Indicates whether the provider is specifically excluded from the Medicaid program. A True value requires notification to the state Medicaid agency and termination of Medicaid billing privileges. State-level exclusions may apply even when federal OIG exclusion is not in effect.
reference: CMS Conditions of Participation; OIG Exclusion Program; State Departments of Health

description: Indicates whether the provider is specifically excluded from the Medicare program. A True value requires immediate termination of Medicare billing privileges and prohibits the organization from employing or contracting with the excluded individual in any capacity paid by Medicare.
reference: CMS Conditions of Participation; OIG Exclusion Program; Social Security Act § 1128

description: Free-text field for additional context, compliance officer observations, legal counsel notes, or supplementary information related to the sanction that is not captured in structured fields. Used by credentialing and compliance staff for case management.
reference: Symplr Credentialing; OIG Compliance Program Guidance

description: The date on which notifications regarding the sanction were dispatched to required internal and external parties. Used for compliance audit trails demonstrating timely adverse action response.
reference: CMS Conditions of Participation; The Joint Commission (TJC); NPDB

description: Indicates whether the required notifications have been sent to relevant internal stakeholders (medical staff office, department chief, compliance officer, revenue cycle) and external parties (payers, state licensing boards) following identification of the sanction.
reference: CMS Conditions of Participation; The Joint Commission (TJC); OIG Compliance Program Guidance

description: The date on which the adverse action was reported to the National Practitioner Data Bank. Must occur within 30 days of the action per HCQIA requirements. Null if not yet reported or reporting is not required for this sanction type.
reference: NPDB; Health Care Quality Improvement Act (HCQIA) 42 U.S.C. § 11101

business_glossary_term: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Report Number
description: The unique report identifier assigned by the National Practitioner Data Bank when the adverse action was reported. Required for NPDB query and response matching, credentialing verification, and mandatory adverse action reporting compliance under HCQIA.
reference: NPDB; Health Care Quality Improvement Act (HCQIA) 42 U.S.C. § 11101

description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier assigned by CMS to the sanctioned provider. Required for OIG exclusion screening, NPDB adverse action reporting, and payer enrollment verification. Stored directly on the sanction record to preserve the identifier at the time of the adverse action.
reference: CMS NPI Registry; HIPAA Administrative Simplification 45 CFR Part 162

description: Indicates whether the sanction has triggered or is expected to trigger termination or suspension of the provider's payer enrollment with one or more health plans or government programs. True initiates payer notification workflows and revenue cycle impact assessment.
reference: CMS Conditions of Participation; OIG Exclusion Program; Symplr Provider Enrollment

description: Indicates whether the provider's clinical privileges at the organization's facilities have been suspended as a direct result of this sanction. Distinct from credentialing_hold, which applies to new or renewal applications. True requires immediate notification to department chiefs and medical staff office.
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) Medical Staff Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation; HCQIA

description: Indicates whether the sanctioned entity is an individual clinician (physician, nurse, allied health professional) or an organizational provider (hospital, group practice, DME supplier). Determines applicable screening rules, reporting obligations, and credentialing workflows.
reference: CMS NPI Registry; OIG Exclusion Program; NPDB

description: Narrative description of the basis or grounds for the adverse action as stated by the issuing authority. May include fraud, abuse, patient harm, controlled substance violations, billing irregularities, or professional misconduct. Used for credentialing review, CDI, and fraud and abuse prevention analysis.
reference: OIG Exclusion Program; False Claims Act 31 U.S.C. § 3729; DEA; State Medical Board Standards

description: Standardized code representing the category of misconduct or violation that led to the sanction, as defined by the issuing authority or NPDB classification scheme (e.g., OIG exclusion basis codes: 1128a, 1128b). Enables structured analytics and regulatory reporting across sanction types.
reference: NPDB; OIG Exclusion Program; Social Security Act § 1128

description: The date on which the provider was formally reinstated or restored to good standing by the issuing authority following completion of the sanction period or successful appeal. Null if the sanction is still active or has not been lifted.
reference: OIG Exclusion Program; NPDB; CMS Conditions of Participation

business_glossary_term: Reported to National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Flag
description: Indicates whether the adverse action has been reported to the National Practitioner Data Bank as required under the Health Care Quality Improvement Act. Mandatory reporting is required for clinical privilege actions, professional society membership actions, and certain licensure actions.

description: The official effective date on which the sanction, exclusion, or adverse action was imposed by the issuing authority. This is the principal business event date used for OIG exclusion screening compliance, credentialing holds, and False Claims Act liability calculations.

description: Current lifecycle state of the sanction record. Active indicates the adverse action is in force; reinstated indicates the provider has been restored; expired indicates the sanction period has lapsed; appealed indicates a formal challenge is pending; withdrawn indicates the issuing authority rescinded the action.
