description: Indicates whether the provider's state medical license has been verified as current and in good standing through primary source verification (PSV) during this reappointment cycle.
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.06.01.05; NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 1; URAC Credentialing Standards

description: Dollar amount of professional liability (malpractice) insurance coverage per occurrence as verified during this reappointment cycle. Compared against facility-required minimums.
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.06.01.05; NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 8

description: Indicates whether the provider's professional liability (malpractice) insurance coverage has been verified as meeting facility minimum requirements during this reappointment cycle.
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.06.01.05; NCQA Credentialing Standards CR 8

description: Category of medical staff membership being reappointed (e.g., Active, Associate, Courtesy, Consulting). Determines voting rights, call obligations, and scope of privileges. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|associate|courtesy|consulting|honorary|affiliate — promote to reference product]
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.01.01.01; CMS 42 CFR §482.22

description: Expiration date of the newly granted appointment term resulting from this reappointment. Typically two years from the effective date per Joint Commission standards.

business_glossary_term: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Adverse Finding Flag
description: Indicates whether the NPDB query returned any adverse action reports, malpractice payment history, or licensure actions for this provider. Triggers mandatory committee review and potential conditions on reappointment.
reference: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Guidebook; Health Care Quality Improvement Act (HCQIA) §11135

business_glossary_term: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Queried Flag
description: Indicates whether the National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) was queried for adverse action reports, malpractice payment reports, and licensure actions during this reappointment cycle. Mandatory query per HCQIA for all reappointments.
reference: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Guidebook; Health Care Quality Improvement Act (HCQIA) §11135; CMS 42 CFR §482.22

business_glossary_term: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Query Date
description: Date on which the NPDB was queried for this provider during the reappointment cycle. Must be within the credentialing review window to satisfy regulatory requirements.
reference: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Guidebook; Health Care Quality Improvement Act (HCQIA) §11135

business_glossary_term: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Report Date
description: Date on which the adverse action report was submitted to the NPDB following a denial or adverse reappointment decision. Must be submitted within 30 days of the final decision per HCQIA requirements.
reference: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Guidebook; Health Care Quality Improvement Act (HCQIA) §11133

business_glossary_term: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Report Required Flag
description: Indicates whether an adverse action report must be submitted to the NPDB as a result of this reappointment decision (e.g., denial, voluntary surrender of privileges during investigation). Mandatory reporting obligation under HCQIA.
reference: National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Guidebook; Health Care Quality Improvement Act (HCQIA) §11133; CMS 42 CFR §482.22

description: Externally visible, human-readable business identifier for the reappointment cycle record, used in correspondence, committee agendas, and credentialing file references (e.g., REAPPT-2024-000123).
reference: Symplr Credentialing; The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.06.01.05

business_glossary_term: Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE) Performance Rating
description: Overall performance rating assigned during the most recent OPPE review cycle. Summarizes clinical quality, patient safety, and professional conduct indicators evaluated during the review period.
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.08.01.01 — Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE)

business_glossary_term: Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE) Review Date
description: Date of the most recent Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE) completed for this provider prior to the reappointment decision. OPPE data is a required input to the reappointment process per Joint Commission standards.
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.08.01.01 — Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE)

description: Narrative summary of the peer review findings conducted during the reappointment review period. Synthesizes Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE) and Focused Professional Practice Evaluation (FPPE) results. Protected under state peer review privilege statutes.
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.08.01.01 (OPPE); MS.08.01.03 (FPPE); State Peer Review Protection Statutes

description: Indicates whether the provider met all required quality performance indicators (e.g., core measures, HEDIS metrics, VBP benchmarks) during the review period. A value of False may trigger additional review or conditions on reappointment.
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.06.01.05; CMS Value-Based Purchasing (VBP); NCQA HEDIS

description: Current lifecycle state of the reappointment application. Tracks progression from initiation through committee review to final decision. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|in_review|approved|denied|deferred|withdrawn — promote to reference product if additional statuses are needed]
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.06.01.05; Symplr Credentialing Workflow

description: End date of the clinical performance review period evaluated during this reappointment cycle. Marks the close of the data collection window for quality indicators and peer review.
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.06.01.05; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: Start date of the clinical performance review period evaluated during this reappointment cycle. Typically covers the prior two years of practice activity at the facility.
reference: The Joint Commission (TJC) MS.06.01.05; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: Indicates whether OIG exclusion list, SAM.gov, and state Medicaid exclusion database checks were completed for this provider during the reappointment cycle. Mandatory for participation in federal healthcare programs.
reference: Office of Inspector General (OIG) — List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE); SAM.gov; CMS 42 CFR §1001

description: Date on which the OIG exclusion list and related sanctions database checks were completed for this provider during the reappointment cycle.
reference: Office of Inspector General (OIG) — LEIE; SAM.gov; CMS 42 CFR §1001

description: Indicates whether any active OIG exclusion, SAM.gov debarment, or state Medicaid exclusion was identified during the sanctions check. A True value mandates immediate escalation and precludes reappointment.
reference: Office of Inspector General (OIG) — LEIE; CMS 42 CFR §1001; State Medicaid Exclusion Databases

description: Native record identifier from the originating operational system (e.g., Symplr reappointment record ID). Enables traceability and reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and the source system of record.
reference: Symplr Credentialing; ETL Data Lineage Standards; ISO 27001

description: Timestamp when this reappointment record was last modified in the data platform. Used for change detection, incremental ETL processing, and audit trail maintenance.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b) — Audit Controls; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF

business_glossary_term: Study Team Member - Study Team Member Id
description: Primary key for the study_team_member association
Foreign key linking to the clinician serving as a member of the research study team. References the provider domain master record for the healthcare professional.

business_glossary_term: Study Team Member - Research Study Id
description: Foreign key linking to the research study for which the clinician is a team member. References the research domain master record for the study.

Current lifecycle status of this study team member assignment. Active indicates the clinician is currently performing study duties. Inactive or Terminated indicates the assignment has ended. Pending Approval indicates the assignment is awaiting IRB or institutional approval. Used for operational reporting, access control, and regulatory compliance.

The date on which the clinician submitted their conflict of interest disclosure for this study. Used to track timeliness of disclosure (must be before study involvement begins) and to determine when annual updates are due.

Indicates whether the clinician has completed conflict of interest disclosure for this specific study assignment. Required for federally-funded research and industry-sponsored trials. Tracks compliance with institutional COI policy and PHS/NIH financial conflict of interest regulations.
reference: 42 CFR Part 50 Subpart F, 45 CFR Part 94

description: Indicates whether this clinician is serving in a study coordination role (research coordinator, research nurse, clinical research associate). Coordinators manage day-to-day study operations, subject recruitment, data collection, and regulatory documentation. Used for workload balancing, training requirements, and operational reporting.

The date on which the clinician signed the study delegation of authority log, acknowledging their assigned responsibilities and confirming they have the training, education, and experience to perform delegated tasks. Required for GCP compliance and regulatory inspections. Nullable if role does not require delegation log signature.

The percentage of the clinician's professional time allocated to this specific research study. Required for NIH effort reporting, institutional cost accounting, and conflict of commitment assessment. Sum of effort_percentage across all concurrent studies for a clinician should not exceed 100%. Used in grant budget justification and progress reports.

The date on which the clinician ceased serving in this role on the research study team. Nullable for currently active team members. Used for regulatory compliance, effort reporting closeout, and historical accountability. Triggers Form 1572 updates and IRB amendment notifications when key personnel depart.

The date on which the clinician signed FDA Form 1572 (Statement of Investigator) for this study. Required for Principal Investigators and sub-investigators on IND studies. Documents commitment to conduct the study per protocol, comply with FDA regulations, and report adverse events. Critical for regulatory compliance and inspection readiness.

The date on which the clinician completed Good Clinical Practice (GCP) training that is current and valid for this study assignment. GCP training is required for all research personnel involved in clinical trials. Must be completed before study responsibilities begin and renewed per institutional policy (typically every 2-3 years).

Indicates whether this clinician is the Principal Investigator (PI) for this study. Only one team member per study should have this flag set to true. The PI has ultimate responsibility for study conduct, regulatory compliance, and scientific integrity. Used for signature routing, regulatory submissions, and accountability reporting.

The date on which the clinician completed training specific to this research study protocol, including study objectives, procedures, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and safety monitoring. Required before performing any study procedures. Documented for regulatory compliance and inspection readiness.

The specific role or function the clinician performs on the research study team. Critical for regulatory compliance (FDA Form 1572 requires listing of investigators and sub-investigators), delegation of authority logs, and role-based access control in research systems. Drives workflow routing, signature authority, and audit trail requirements.

The date on which the clinician officially began serving in this role on the research study team. Used for regulatory compliance (Form 1572 effective dates), effort reporting period determination, and conflict of interest disclosure timing. Must align with IRB approval of personnel changes and completion of required training.

Indicates whether this clinician is designated as a sub-investigator with delegated study responsibilities. Sub-investigators must be listed on FDA Form 1572 and have documented delegation of specific protocol procedures. Used for regulatory compliance, delegation log management, and signature authority determination.
Unique system-generated identifier for each clinician participation record in an accreditation survey
Foreign key linking to the accreditation survey event in which the clinician participated
Foreign key linking to the clinician who participated in the accreditation survey

Number of survey findings or observations attributed to this clinician's area of responsibility, interview responses, or care delivery during tracer review. Used for targeted education and performance improvement.
Indicates whether the clinician was formally interviewed by surveyors during this survey event. Used to track interview preparation effectiveness and staff readiness.
Total duration in minutes of formal surveyor interviews with this clinician during the survey event. Used for survey burden analysis and staff time allocation.

Free-text notes capturing specific observations, surveyor feedback, areas of strength, or improvement opportunities identified during this clinician's survey participation. Used for debriefing and continuous improvement.

The specific date on which this clinician participated in survey activities. For multi-day surveys, this captures the day(s) the clinician was involved. Multiple records may exist for the same clinician-survey pair if they participated on different days or in different roles.

Internal quality team assessment of the clinician's performance during survey participation, including interview responses, documentation quality, and adherence to standards. Used for recognition and targeted coaching.
Indicates whether the clinician completed required survey readiness training and preparation activities prior to the survey event. Used to correlate preparation with survey performance.

The specific role or capacity in which the clinician participated in the accreditation survey. Examples include interviewed staff member, department head representing a service line, tracer participant whose patient care was reviewed, or subject matter expert consulted during standards review.

Indicates whether the clinician participated in a tracer methodology session where surveyors followed a patient through their care journey and interviewed care team members. Critical for tracer preparation and performance analysis.
Unique surrogate identifier for each telehealth authorization record. Primary key for the telehealth_authorization data product in the provider domain.
Reference to the healthcare facility (distant site) from which the clinician delivers telehealth services under this authorization. Links to the provider.org_provider or facility master record.
reference: CMS Telehealth Policy; 42 CFR §410.78; HL7 FHIR Location Resource

description: Reference to the licensed clinician for whom this telehealth authorization is issued. Links to the provider.clinician master record.

Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_submission. Business justification: Interstate telehealth licenses and compact enrollments are regulatory submissions to state medical boards and compact commissions. Compliance teams track application status, approval dates, and renewa

Foreign key linking to provider.credentialing_application. Business justification: Telehealth authorizations may be part of credentialing process. FK will be NULL for authorizations obtained independently. No redundant columns to remove.

Reference to the credentialing file or record in the credentialing management system (e.g., Symplr) that contains supporting documentation for this telehealth authorization, including primary source verification artifacts.
reference: Symplr Credentialing; NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission (TJC)

description: FK to provider.specialty
The date on which the clinician or their credentialing team submitted the application for this telehealth authorization to the relevant state board or compact administrator.
The date on which the issuing authority (state licensing board, compact administrator, or federal agency) formally approved this telehealth authorization.
reference: Symplr Credentialing; State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing

description: Indicates whether this authorization permits audio-only (telephone) telehealth encounters in addition to or instead of video-based encounters. CMS and many states have specific rules governing audio-only telehealth reimbursement.
reference: CMS Telehealth Policy; 42 CFR §410.78; State Departments of Health

description: Externally assigned or internally generated unique reference number for this telehealth authorization, used for tracking and correspondence with state licensing boards, payers, and interstate compact administrators.
reference: Interstate Medical Licensure Compact (IMLC); CMS Telehealth Policy

description: Current lifecycle state of the telehealth authorization. Active indicates the clinician is currently authorized to deliver telehealth in the distant state. Pending indicates application submitted but not yet approved. Expired, suspended, and revoked indicate the authorization is no longer valid.
reference: CMS Telehealth Policy; State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing; HIPAA 45 CFR §164

description: Classification of the legal basis under which the clinician is authorized to deliver telehealth services across state lines. Values include state_license (full state license in distant state), interstate_compact (IMLC or PSYPACT membership), federal_waiver (CMS or DEA waiver), reciprocity_agreement (bilateral state agreement), or emergency_waiver (public health emergency authorization).
reference: Interstate Medical Licensure Compact (IMLC); PSYPACT; CMS Telehealth Waivers; 42 CFR §410.78

business_glossary_term: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Telehealth Eligibility Indicator
description: Indicates whether the clinician is eligible to bill Medicare and Medicaid for telehealth services under this authorization per CMS telehealth coverage rules (42 CFR §410.78). True = CMS-eligible telehealth provider; False = not eligible for CMS telehealth reimbursement under this authorization.
reference: 42 CFR §410.78; CMS Telehealth Policy; Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS)

description: Unique membership or registration identifier assigned by the interstate compact administrator (e.g., IMLC, PSYPACT, NLC) when the clinician is authorized under a compact rather than a full state license. Null if authorization_type is not interstate_compact.
reference: Interstate Medical Licensure Compact (IMLC); PSYPACT; Nurse Licensure Compact (NLC)

description: Identifies the specific interstate compact program under which this authorization is granted. IMLC = Interstate Medical Licensure Compact (physicians), PSYPACT = Psychology Interjurisdictional Compact, NLC = Nurse Licensure Compact, ASLP-IC = Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact, PT_Compact = Physical Therapy Compact, OT_Compact = Occupational Therapy Compact. Null or 'none' if not compact-based. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IMLC|PSYPACT|NLC|ASLP-IC|PT_Compact|OT_Compact|none — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: Interstate Medical Licensure Compact (IMLC); PSYPACT; Nurse Licensure Compact (NLC); ASLP-IC; PT Compact

business_glossary_term: Controlled Substance Prescribing Allowed via Telehealth
description: Indicates whether the clinician is authorized to prescribe controlled substances via telehealth under this authorization. Governed by the Ryan Haight Act, DEA telemedicine rules, and applicable state law. Critical for pharmacy compliance and MAR (Medication Administration Record) workflows.
reference: DEA — Controlled Substances; Ryan Haight Online Pharmacy Consumer Protection Act; 21 CFR §1306

description: The timestamp when this telehealth authorization record was first created in the data platform. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and compliance reporting.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR §164; ISO 27001 — Information Security Management; Internal Data Governance Standard

description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for international telehealth authorizations where the clinician or patient is located outside the United States. Null for domestic (US-only) authorizations.
reference: ISO 3166-1; HHS International Telehealth Guidance; HIPAA 45 CFR §164

description: Two-letter US state code representing the state where the clinician (distant site) is physically located and licensed when delivering telehealth services. The clinician must hold valid authorization to practice in this state.
reference: 42 CFR §410.78; CMS Telehealth Policy; Interstate Medical Licensure Compact (IMLC)

description: The date on which this telehealth authorization becomes legally effective and the clinician is permitted to deliver virtual care services under its terms.
reference: CMS Telehealth Policy; State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing

description: Indicates whether an automated expiration alert notification has been sent to the clinician and credentialing team for this telehealth authorization. Used to track renewal workflow initiation.
reference: Symplr Credentialing; Internal Credentialing Workflow Policy

description: The date on which this telehealth authorization expires and the clinician is no longer authorized to deliver telehealth services under this authorization. Null for open-ended or indefinite authorizations.
reference: CMS Telehealth Policy; State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: Name of the regulatory body, state licensing board, or compact administrator that issued this telehealth authorization (e.g., 'California Medical Board', 'Interstate Medical Licensure Compact Commission', 'CMS', 'DEA').
reference: State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing; CMS; Interstate Medical Licensure Compact (IMLC)

description: Indicates whether the clinician is eligible to bill Medicaid in the distant state for telehealth services under this authorization. Medicaid telehealth policies vary by state and are distinct from Medicare eligibility.
reference: CMS Medicaid Telehealth Policy; State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing

description: Indicates whether the clinician is participating in-network for telehealth services in the distant state under this authorization. Relevant for payer contracting, patient cost-sharing, and ACO/HMO/PPO network management.
reference: CMS Telehealth Policy; NCQA Credentialing Standards; Symplr Provider Enrollment

description: Free-text field for credentialing staff to capture additional context, conditions, or remarks associated with this telehealth authorization that are not captured in structured fields (e.g., special conditions imposed by the issuing authority, internal compliance notes).
reference: Symplr Credentialing; Internal Credentialing Workflow Policy

description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the clinician as assigned by CMS. Required for telehealth billing and payer enrollment verification. Stored here for authorization record completeness and cross-referencing with payer systems.
reference: CMS NPI Registry; HIPAA 45 CFR §162.406; HL7 FHIR Practitioner Resource

description: Two-letter US state code representing the state where the patient (originating site) is physically located at the time of the telehealth encounter. Per CMS telehealth rules, the originating state determines applicable licensure and coverage requirements.
reference: 42 CFR §410.78; CMS Telehealth Policy; FHIR R4 Location Resource

description: The date on which the clinician was successfully enrolled with payers for telehealth billing in the distant state under this authorization.
reference: CMS Provider Enrollment; Symplr Provider Enrollment

description: Indicates the clinician's enrollment status with payers for telehealth billing in the distant state. Enrolled = active payer enrollment for telehealth services; Pending = enrollment application submitted; Not_enrolled = not yet enrolled; Terminated = enrollment ended.
reference: CMS Provider Enrollment; Symplr Provider Enrollment; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: Specifies any restrictions on the telehealth delivery platform permitted under this authorization (e.g., 'HIPAA-compliant video only', 'audio-only prohibited', 'Epic MyChart only', 'no consumer-grade platforms'). Null if no platform restrictions apply. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product if standardized platform list is maintained]
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR §164; OCR HIPAA Telehealth Guidance; CMS Telehealth Policy

description: The standard renewal cycle in months for this telehealth authorization as defined by the issuing authority (e.g., 12, 24, 36 months). Used to calculate the next renewal_date and schedule credentialing workflow triggers.
reference: State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: The date on which the clinician must submit a renewal application to maintain continuity of this telehealth authorization. Used to trigger credentialing workflow alerts.
reference: Symplr Credentialing; NCQA Credentialing Standards; CMS Telehealth Policy

description: The date on which this telehealth authorization was permanently revoked by the issuing authority. Null if the authorization has not been revoked.
reference: State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing; OIG — Fraud and Abuse; NPDB

description: Free-text description of the reason this telehealth authorization was revoked, as documented by the issuing authority or the organization's credentialing team.
reference: State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing; OIG — Fraud and Abuse; NPDB

description: Describes any restrictions on the types of clinical services permitted under this telehealth authorization (e.g., 'behavioral health only', 'chronic disease management only', 'no controlled substance prescribing', 'no new patient encounters'). Null if no service restrictions apply.
reference: CMS Telehealth Policy; DEA Telemedicine Prescribing Rules; State Departments of Health

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this telehealth authorization record was sourced (e.g., Symplr Credentialing, Epic, Cerner, MEDITECH, or manual entry). Used for ETL lineage and data reconciliation.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; Symplr Credentialing; Epic EHR

description: The native record identifier from the source operational system (e.g., Symplr authorization record ID, Epic provider record ID) for this telehealth authorization. Enables traceability and reconciliation back to the system of record.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; Symplr Credentialing

description: The clinician's license number issued by the distant state licensing board that underpins this telehealth authorization. Applicable when authorization_type is 'state_license' or 'reciprocity_agreement'.
reference: State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: The date on which this telehealth authorization was suspended by the issuing authority or internally by the organization. Null if the authorization has never been suspended.
reference: State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing; OIG — Fraud and Abuse

description: Free-text description of the reason this telehealth authorization was suspended, as documented by the issuing authority or the organization's credentialing team.
reference: State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing; OIG — Fraud and Abuse

description: The timestamp when this telehealth authorization record was last modified in the data platform. Used for change tracking, incremental ETL processing, and audit compliance.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR §164; ISO 27001 — Information Security Management; Internal Data Governance Standard

description: The date on which primary source verification of this telehealth authorization was last completed by the credentialing team.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission (TJC)

description: Method used to perform primary source verification of this telehealth authorization. Online_portal = state board website; Phone = direct call to issuing authority; Written_confirmation = letter or fax; Third_party_service = CAQH ProView or similar; CAQH = Council for Affordable Quality Healthcare attestation.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; CAQH ProView; The Joint Commission (TJC)

description: Status of primary source verification for this telehealth authorization. Verified = confirmed directly with issuing authority; Pending = verification in progress; Failed = could not be verified; Not_required = exempt from PSV per policy.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission (TJC); Symplr Credentialing

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each provider network affiliation record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
Reference to the specific facility or practice location at which the provider participates in this network. A provider may have multiple network affiliations at different facility locations.
reference: CMS Facility Enrollment; CMS Provider Directory Requirements; 45 CFR 156.230

description: Reference to the individual clinician or organizational provider associated with this network affiliation record. Links to the provider master entity.

Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_submission. Business justification: Network participation changes require regulatory notification (state Medicaid network adequacy reporting, quarterly network roster submissions). Compliance teams track submission status and acknowledg

Reference to the medical group or group practice through which the individual provider participates in this network. Many payer contracts are held at the group level, with individual providers enrolled under the group.
reference: CMS Group Practice Enrollment; NPI Type 2 (Organizational NPI); CAQH ProView

description: Foreign key linking to provider.org_provider. Business justification: Organizational providers have network affiliations in addition to individual clinicians. FK will be NULL for clinician-only affiliations. No redundant columns to remove.
Identifier of the provider contract or participation agreement governing the terms of this network affiliation, including reimbursement rates and obligations. Links to the contract management system.
reference: CMS Provider Contracting; OIG Compliance; NCQA Standards

description: Reference to the health insurance payer or managed care organization that owns or administers the network to which the provider is affiliated.
Reference to the specific payer network or care network (ACO, HMO, PPO, POS) to which the provider is affiliated.
The payer-assigned enrollment or provider identification number issued upon successful enrollment in the network. Used for claims submission and remittance matching. Distinct from NPI.
reference: CMS Provider Enrollment; CAQH ProView; Symplr Provider Enrollment

description: Foreign key linking to provider.specialty. Business justification: Network participation is specialty-specific. network_affiliation.specialty_code and specialty_description should reference specialty table.

Indicates whether the provider is currently accepting new patients within this network. Distinct from panel_status in that it reflects the provider's current operational availability rather than the formal panel designation.
reference: CMS Network Adequacy; CMS Provider Directory Requirements; 45 CFR 156.230

description: Indicates whether the provider is a participating member of an Accountable Care Organization (ACO) under this network affiliation. ACO participation drives shared savings calculations and quality reporting under CMS MSSP and Next Gen ACO programs.
reference: CMS Medicare Shared Savings Program (MSSP); 42 CFR 425; CMS ACO Regulations

description: Current lifecycle status of the provider's network affiliation. 'active' indicates the provider is currently participating and eligible to see network patients. 'pending' indicates enrollment is in process. 'suspended' indicates temporary hold pending investigation or credentialing review.
reference: CMS Provider Enrollment; Symplr Credentialing; CAQH ProView

description: Maximum patient age (in years) that the provider accepts within this network affiliation. Null indicates no upper age limit. Used for provider directory filtering and patient-to-provider matching.
reference: CMS Provider Directory Requirements; NCQA Standards

description: Minimum patient age (in years) that the provider accepts within this network affiliation. Used for provider directory filtering and patient-to-provider matching in managed care systems.
reference: CMS Provider Directory Requirements; NCQA Standards

description: Date on which the provider's credentialing with this network expires and re-credentialing must be completed. Typically occurs every two years per NCQA standards. Used to trigger re-credentialing workflows.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06; Symplr Credentialing

description: Current credentialing status of the provider with the payer or network organization. Credentialing must be completed before a provider can be listed as in-network. Tracked via Symplr or CAQH ProView.
reference: NCQA Credentialing Standards; The Joint Commission MS.06; Symplr Credentialing; CAQH ProView

description: Indicates whether this provider network affiliation record has been published in the payer's public-facing provider directory. CMS requires accurate and up-to-date provider directories for all Medicare Advantage and Marketplace plans.
reference: CMS Provider Directory Requirements; 42 CFR 422.111; 45 CFR 156.230

description: The date on which the provider's participation in the network becomes effective and the provider is eligible to see in-network patients. Used for claims adjudication and provider directory accuracy.
reference: CMS Provider Enrollment; 42 CFR 422.204; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: Indicates the patient gender population served by the provider within this network (e.g., all genders, male only, female only, pediatric). Used for provider directory accuracy and patient matching.
reference: CMS Provider Directory Requirements; ACA Section 1557; NCQA Standards

description: Description of the geographic region or service area covered by this network affiliation (e.g., state name, county, metropolitan statistical area, or CMS-defined service area). Used for network adequacy geographic analysis and CMS service area filings.
reference: CMS Network Adequacy Geographic Standards; 42 CFR 422.112; 45 CFR 156.230

description: Indicates whether the provider's practice location associated with this network affiliation is handicap accessible per ADA requirements. Required for CMS provider directory accuracy and ADA compliance reporting.
reference: Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA); CMS Provider Directory Requirements; Section 504 Rehabilitation Act

description: Indicates whether this network affiliation record pertains to a hospital or facility provider (as opposed to an individual clinician). Used to distinguish facility-level from practitioner-level network participation in directory and adequacy reporting.
reference: CMS Provider Directory Requirements; NCQA Credentialing Standards

description: Comma-separated list of languages spoken by the provider at this network location, using ISO 639-1 language codes. Required for provider directory accuracy and CMS language access compliance under Section 1557 of the ACA.
reference: ACA Section 1557; CMS Provider Directory Requirements; ISO 639-1

description: Date on which the network affiliation information was last verified against the payer's provider directory or credentialing source. CMS requires provider directories to be updated at least every 90 days.
reference: CMS Provider Directory Requirements; 42 CFR 422.111; 45 CFR 156.230; NCQA Standards

business_glossary_term: Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS) Eligible Flag
description: Indicates whether the provider is eligible for Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS) reporting under this network affiliation. MIPS eligibility affects payment adjustments under MACRA and is tracked at the provider-payer level.
reference: CMS MIPS; MACRA 42 CFR 414 Subpart O; CMS Quality Payment Program

description: Provider category used for CMS and state network adequacy analysis. Classifies the provider's role in meeting time-and-distance and appointment availability standards required for network certification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: primary_care|specialist|behavioral_health|hospital|ancillary|pharmacy — promote to reference product if additional categories are needed]
reference: CMS Network Adequacy Standards; 45 CFR 156.230; 42 CFR 422.112; NCQA Standards

description: Tiered network designation indicating the provider's cost and quality tier within the payer's network structure. Tier 1 typically represents highest-value providers with lowest patient cost-sharing; higher tiers carry greater patient out-of-pocket costs.
reference: CMS Tiered Network Standards; NCQA Network Adequacy; 45 CFR 156.230

description: Free-text field for operational notes or comments related to this network affiliation record, such as special contract terms, exceptions, or credentialing remarks entered by network management staff.
